issues.issue_title: [BUG] Git tag handling regression in 6.14.5
issues.body:
# What / Why
NPM 6.14.5 and 6.15.6 have a regression in handling of git tags.

## How

### Current Behavior
Under 6.14.4 if you add a package from a specific git tag, run install, then change the tag in package.json,
and run install again, the package gets updated.

Under 6.15.5

### Steps to Reproduce

The following example use pacote, not because it is realistic, since all its tags are published versions,
but because I know it is publicly accessible, and it can still show off the problem.

<!-- Describe how to produce the issue -->
* git init
* echo
* npm init
* npm i https://github.com/npm/pacote#v11.1.7
* git add .
* git commit -m 'test'
* edit package.json and change the tag to `#v11.1.8`
* npm i
* git diff

Notice that the package and lock file were not updated if using 6.14.5 or 6.14.6.

### Expected Behavior
Same as 6.14.4: Package and package-lock.json are updated, the same as if I changed the a normal version number to something incompatible with the version specified in package-lock.json.

## References
I suspect the cause is a side effect of the change to the `childDependencySpecifier` call in PR #758:
https://github.com/npm/cli/commit/33ec41f18f557146607cb14a7a38c707fce6d42c#diff-5081bd1aabac431eccfb75bfa08bde1bL573

If I recall correctly, the `_from` value was used to determine if the git branch specified in the package-lock.json actually matches what is specified in package.json. Not passing in that information breaks this check.

issues.issue_title: Cannot inject JhiLanguageService into any core component
issues.body:
##### **Overview of the issue** Regarding the Angular template: Cannot inject `JhiLanguageService` into any core component. As far as I see, as soon as `JhiLanguageService` is injected into any eagerly bootstrapped component, the app does not work anymore. More precisely, within `AccountService.fetch()` `this.languageService` is undefined which causes any authentication to fail. ##### **Motivation for or Use Case** What we try to achieve is, while loading the application, to set the language to the current browser language. Out attempt was to add the following to `JhiMainComponent`: ``` export class JhiMainComponent implements OnInit { constructor( ... private translateService: TranslateService, private languageService: JhiLanguageService) {} ngOnInit() { ... const languageKey = this.translateService.getBrowserLang(); this.languageService.changeLanguage(languageKey); } } ``` ##### **Reproduce the error** Create a new JHipster 6.3.1 application with the `angular` template. Then add the above lines to `JhiMainComponent`. ##### **Suggest a Fix** As far as I see, the problem is that the constructor of `JhiLanguageService` calls `this.translateService.setDefaultLang(this.currentLang)` which in turn tries to load the language from the backend via HTTP. However due to the registered ``` { provide: HTTP_INTERCEPTORS, useClass: AuthExpiredInterceptor, multi: true } ``` that in turn demands ``` constructor(private loginService: LoginService) ``` where `LoginService` demands ``` constructor(private accountService: AccountService, private authServerProvider: AuthServerProvider) {} ``` and `AccountService` in turn demands ``` constructor(private languageService: JhiLanguageService, private sessionStorage: SessionStorageService, private http: HttpClient) {} ``` This causes a cyclic dependency ``` JhiLanguageService -> TranslateService -> AuthExpiredInterceptor -> LoginService -> AccountService -> JhiLanguageService ``` Thus the requested `JhiLanguageService` in the constructor of `AccountService` will be undefined and the whole authentication process breaks. I don't know if our approach is wrong here (where to add our default behavior about languages), however the behavior and type of error seems something unwanted. The only solutions I can think of is either * switch the language later / lazily (where would be the best place to do this?) * bypass the interceptors to load languages for internationalization (it does not seem useful to pass through an `AuthExpiredInterceptor` when loading languages that you need before the login has ever passed) ##### **JHipster Version(s)** 6.3.1 ##### **JHipster configuration** jhipster info INFO! [Acces to Principal outside the 'router-outlet' in main component in JHipster Angular](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/53587152/acces-to-principal-outside-the-router-outlet-in-main-component-in-jhipster-ang)

> I can inject the Principal in any component rendered inside the router-outlet, however, if i try to inject it in the main component, an error is shown whenever i try to login/logout (if i refresh the page everything shows fine).

In the end I created another service:

- create a service with the variables
- inject this service in the main component
- edited the login service

> bypass the interceptors to load languages for internationalization (it does not seem useful to pass through an AuthExpiredInterceptor when loading languages that you need before the login has ever passed)

I am not clear on this as you should be able to load languages resource bundle as those are not protected by login and associated interceptors. You can follow same by manually changing language in the drop down (before login). Initial language bundle chosen on the application load is specified by `defaultI18nLang: 'en'` in core module. In case, you want to change to browser default, then, you need to change here.

@vishal423 submitted a good answer.

Just FYI I add comment about my investigation results.

Seems that this comes from Angular HTTP interceptors DI problem.

I debugged HTTP interceptors part and found out that:
* in the current code all HTTP interceptors are constructed twice
* after adding `JhiLanguageService` to `MainComponent` all HTTP interceptors are constructed once

I debugged `AuthExpiredInterceptor` and related services DI and found out that:
* `loginService` in `AuthExpiredInterceptor`:
    * in the current code: `undefined` in the first execution of the constructor, correct value in the second execution of the constructor, Angular issue which deals with a similar topic: https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/25590
    * after using `JhiLanguageService` in the `MainComponent`, `loginService` has correct value in the only execution of the constructor
* `LoginService` is always constructed once and `accountService` has correct value both in the current code and after using `JhiLanguageService` in the `MainComponent`
* `AccountService` is always constructed once and `languageService` in the `AccountService` constructor:
    * in the current code is available in the constructor
    * after using `JhiLanguageService` in the `MainComponent` is `undefined` in the constructor. Seems that Angular is able to cure HTTP interceptors dependencies if they are `undefined` (by recreating interceptors) but not nested services dependencies.

More than 1 workaround exist to that Angular HTTP interceptors DI problem. Below 2 possible workarounds.

Workaround 1: add `JhiLanguageService` to app module `providers` array before HTTP interceptors, after that `JhiLanguageService` is always available in HTTP interceptors DI.

Workaround 2: as `JhiLanguageService` is not needed in `AccountService` constructor then you can get it from `Injector` just before using that (as @codecholeric described in the previous comment), but I believe that more optimized code for that is:
```
if (this.languageService === undefined) {
  this.languageService = this.injector.get(JhiLanguageService);
}
```
I raised PR-s jhipster/ng-jhipster#110 and #10492 to fix this issue.
@kaidohallik thank you so much for fixing this so quickly, I really appreciate it :smile:

issues.issue_title: version 3.3.2 is a breaking change
issues.body:
Hello,

`Version 3.3.2` requires `Node ">= 20"`.
For projects relying on semver ranges this will break their installation if they are on Node < 20 (ie: Node 16.x).

Error:
```
error dompurify@3.3.2: The engine "node" is incompatible with this module. Expected version ">=20". Got "16.15.0"
```

Can we please revert the breaking changes to maintain backwards compatibility in dompurify@3.x versions?

Thanks!

comments.body: Sadly no, EOL releases of NodeJS are not a prio right now.

At my job today we ran into an issue where builds failed in repositories that depend on `jspdf@4`, which in turn caused the deployments to fail. The problem is that `jspdf` declares DOMPurify as an `optionalDependency` with `"^3.3.1"`. Even though it’s optional, npm still installs it, and it resolved to `3.3.2`, which requires Node 20. Since our environments run on Node 16/18, those builds broke.

We don’t use DOMPurify directly, but because it was pulled in through `jspdf`, we had to explicitly install `dompurify@3.3.1` to make things work again.

This is a breaking change that affects projects depending on `jspdf` and still running on older Node versions. Could you please reconsider releasing a `3.3.3` without the Node 20 engine requirement, so these projects don’t hit unexpected failures?

We can probably do that, the relevant change sits [here](https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify/commit/5b69ff63159c92bc4405371ed779e5aecce9bc84), no? 

@Rotzbua as you helped bump the versions, would you know exactly where we'd have to pull the lever?
Yes, that should be the culprit, due to the engines constraint in `package.json`.
@Rotzbua is it safe to just remove it? Don't want to butcher the commit or overlook anything 😅

@cure53 I'll take a look at that after my shift.

If the CI breaks overnight, the fault lies with the CI design. Dependencies should be fixed via lock files in order to achieve a reproducible build.

Thank you and appreciate it 🙂 

> If the CI breaks overnight, the fault lies with the CI design. 

I fully agree, but here we are...

Since 3.3.2 contains security fixes, I think it’s best to keep the current 2.x and 3.x as they are (maintaining those fixes) and handle the Node.js version updates in a new 4.x release.

This way, users who can't upgrade their Node.js environment yet can still benefit from the security patches.

Technically, that sounds reasonable, but we don't have the capacity to maintain even another branch, just because folks decided to have EOL software in their build chain. 

Catering to that circumstance sends bad signals and has the overall security posture deteriorate for no good reason. 

Or, in other words, folks should not expect to be able to run the latest version of security tools if the core is rotten and sitting on top of software that has been dead for three years.

I agree, and I’m not suggesting we maintain old major versions/branches indefinitely.

My point was simply that combining a security fix with a breaking change can often cause confusion for users. I just wanted to highlight that risk from a release management perspective.

@okuryu Fully understood and I agree, but our only angle as a sanitizer maintainer is security. While we need to keep compatibility in mind as well, it is not a priority - and every time we prioritize that, security will lose.

Bottom line, I am open for the 3.3.3 release to fix the current problem, if everyone here agrees as well. Once we are sure what will fit it, I can take care of the rest.

issues.body:
<!-- *Before creating an issue please make sure you are using the latest version of yarn.* -->

**Do you want to request a *feature* or report a *bug*?**

bug

<!-- Is the feature a substantial feature request? Please use https://github.com/yarnpkg/rfcs -->

**What is the current behavior?**

The following package.json

```
{
    "name": "example",
    "version": "0.0.0",
    "dependencies": {
        "example": "link:."
    }
}
```

Produces a heap memory overflow in v8 - possibly due to infinite recursion.

**What is the expected behavior?**

The expected behavior is a link back to ourselves in our `node_modules` folder.

The use case here is to use requires relative to the project root rather than relative paths:

```js
require('example/some/path');
// vs
require('../../../some/path');
```

**Please mention your node.js, yarn and operating system version.**

node v12.10.0, yarn 1.17.3.

This works on yarn 1.3.2 but stops working as of yarn 1.4.0.

issues.issue_title: Custom addContextMenu not working
issues.body:
addContextMenu broke (?) between 5.7.0 and 5.7.1

TinyMCE Fiddle: https://fiddle.tiny.cloud/gohaab

Additional right-click context menu displays on 5.7.0, not on 5.7.1+ (including current version 5.8.1

Probably related to these 'bug fixes':
- Fixed a bug where context menu items with names that contained uppercase characters were not displayed.
- Fixed context menu items lacking support for the disabled and shortcut properties.

(This fiddle is from the tinyMCE blog: https://www.tiny.cloud/blog/tinymce-spellchecker/)

comments.body:
Repro:
- set fiddle to run with TinyMCE 5.7.0
- right-click in editor to see custom context menu
- set fiddle to run with TinyMCE 5.7.1+
- right-click in editor - no custom context menu

Hi @HereThereBDragons, thanks for the report! I can confirm this is working as expected though. The problem is actually in the custom `useBrowserSpellcheck` context menu in the fiddle provided/mentioned in our blog, as its returning invalid data. As per the [documentation](https://www.tiny.cloud/docs/ui-components/contextmenu/#registeringcontextmenusections) the update function should return a string or an array of menu items to show, not a boolean.

So the problem here was that in 5.7.0, it was never using the context menu and was only ever using the regular menu item that used the same name. Now we have two options, we can either remove the context menu altogether which will make it work the same as 5.7.0 or lower, or we can fix the context menu so it does what I believe it was intended to do which is only show when the selection is collapsed. Here's an example: https://fiddle.tiny.cloud/gohaab/9.

Thanks for bringing to our attention that the blog is incorrect! I'll pass this onto the correct team to get the blog post fixed.

Hello @HereThereBDragons, thanks again for bringing this up, I've made the change to our blog post. Thanks to @lnewson for sorting out the solution. The changes should be live now at https://www.tiny.cloud/blog/tinymce-spellchecker/.

issues.issue_title: Timeline onStart/onComplete not being fired correctly when Timeline is empty or has a tween with 0 duration
issues.body:
Hi guys,

I have a Timeline that could be configured with 0 duration Tweens and when I call to Timeline.restart I would expect the timeline to call onStart and onComplete callbacks, but thats is not happening. Also on 3.5.0 only onComplete was called on play and then if you restart the timeline it was not called anymore. And now on 3.6.0 onStart is being called instead of onComplete.

My code depends on the callbacks being called every time the timeline is restarted, what should I do?

comments.body: That was actually a regression in 3.6.0 (it's fixed in the next release). As the docs indicate, an onStart should only fire when the playhead is moved from 0 to something non-zero, but of course that can't happen if you've got a duration of 0. If you really need both callbacks, then don't use a duration of 0. You can make it something like 0.01, for example.
Should be resolved in the latest release.

issues.issue_title: Commit https://github.com/balderdashy/sails/commit/4a023dc5095a4b30fdc8535f705ed34cd22d2f7d breaks websocket sessions
issues.body:
**Node version**: 16.6.0
**Sails version** _(sails)_: 1.5.7
**ORM hook version** _(sails-hook-orm)_: latest
**Sockets hook version** _(sails-hook-sockets)_: latest
**Organics hook version** _(sails-hook-organics)_: Unknown
**Grunt hook version** _(sails-hook-grunt)_: latest
**Uploads hook version** _(sails-hook-uploads)_: Unknown
**DB adapter & version** _(e.g. sails-mysql@5.55.5)_: sails-mysql latest
**Skipper adapter & version** _(e.g. skipper-s3@5.55.5)_: none

Session store: memorystore (also tested flat-file-store)
<hr/>

Commit https://github.com/balderdashy/sails/commit/4a023dc5095a4b30fdc8535f705ed34cd22d2f7d breaks websocket sessions. Namely, req.session is undefined even when a cookie exists in the handshake. Reverting this commit / changes to the req file fixes the problem.

Before knowing the cause of the issue, I attempted a bandage fix by creating a hook to restore req.session if it was undefined. But this did not work; sailsJS was thinking every single API call was a new client, and thus sessions were not persisting / every request had a new session.

Next, I checked cookie parsing. It was correctly receiving the cookie string, but console was outputting an empty object for the cookies. I thought this was weird and thought this was the problem as well. But I looked at the code and saw no reason for it to not work. So I moved on.

I investigated the latest changes, and that's when I noticed the change in virtual req parsing. Since sessions were stored in the req, I decided to see what would happen if I reverted that file to 1.5.6's version. Sure enough, sessions started working again.

issues.issue_title: `pnpm update --filter --latest` leads to the lockfile changing for unrelated project and dependencies, when `dedupe-peer-dependents` is `false`
issues.body:
### Last pnpm version that worked

9.4.0

### pnpm version

9.15.0

### Code to reproduce the issue

More specifically, this stopped working as expected in 9.5.0. Version 10 rc0 also does not work as expected.

I have a full reproduction at https://github.com/fpapado/pnpm-filtered-updated-changes-other-packages, so please refer to that for the full details / a cloneable set of code.

In prose:
You will need a workspace with two packages: `a` and `b`. Each of them depends (pure `dependencies`) on `react@18.3.0`.

Run `pnpm --filter a update --latest react`, to update react only for package `a`, resolving `react@19.0.0`. Optionally run `pnpm install` (the observed behaviour seems the same regardless).

Observe the lockfile diff, see that `react@19.0.0` is resolved also for `b`.  The `package.json` of `b` is unaffected.

```diff
diff --git a/packages/a/package.json b/packages/a/package.json
index 64bd07f..1dfb9e1 100644
--- a/packages/a/package.json
+++ b/packages/a/package.json
@@ -10,6 +10,6 @@
   "author": "",
   "license": "ISC",
   "dependencies": {
-    "react": "18.3.0"
+    "react": "19.0.0"
   }
 }
diff --git a/pnpm-lock.yaml b/pnpm-lock.yaml
index b3fe1d8..0cbf890 100644
--- a/pnpm-lock.yaml
+++ b/pnpm-lock.yaml
@@ -11,36 +11,21 @@ importers:
   packages/a:
     dependencies:
       react:
-        specifier: 18.3.0
-        version: 18.3.0
+        specifier: 19.0.0
+        version: 19.0.0

   packages/b:
     dependencies:
       react:
         specifier: 18.3.0
-        version: 18.3.0
+        version: 19.0.0

 packages:

-  js-tokens@4.0.0:
-    resolution: {integrity: sha512-RdJUflcE3cUzKiMqQgsCu06FPu9UdIJO0beYbPhHN4k6apgJtifcoCtT9bcxOpYBtpD2kCM6Sbzg4CausW/PKQ==}
-
-  loose-envify@1.4.0:
-    resolution: {integrity: sha512-lyuxPGr/Wfhrlem2CL/UcnUc1zcqKAImBDzukY7Y5F/yQiNdko6+fRLevlw1HgMySw7f611UIY408EtxRSoK3Q==}
-    hasBin: true
-
-  react@18.3.0:
-    resolution: {integrity: sha512-RPutkJftSAldDibyrjuku7q11d3oy6wKOyPe5K1HA/HwwrXcEqBdHsLypkC2FFYjP7bPUa6gbzSBhw4sY2JcDg==}
+  react@19.0.0:
+    resolution: {integrity: sha512-V8AVnmPIICiWpGfm6GLzCR/W5FXLchHop40W4nXBmdlEceh16rCN8O8LNWm5bh5XUX91fh7KpA+W0TgMKmgTpQ==}
     engines: {node: '>=0.10.0'}

 snapshots:

-  js-tokens@4.0.0: {}
-
-  loose-envify@1.4.0:
-    dependencies:
-      js-tokens: 4.0.0
-
-  react@18.3.0:
-    dependencies:
-      loose-envify: 1.4.0
+  react@19.0.0: {}
```


`pnpm ls -r react` shows similar output:

```shell
pnpm ls -r react
Legend: production dependency, optional only, dev only

a@1.0.0 /Users/fotis/pnpm-filtered-updated-changes-other-packages/packages/a

dependencies:
react 19.0.0

b@1.0.0 /Users/fotis/pnpm-filtered-updated-changes-other-packages/packages/b

dependencies:
react 19.0.0
```


### Expected behavior

That `a` resolves `react@19.0.0` and `b` resolves `react@18.3.0`

### Actual behavior

Now `a` resolves `react@19.0.0` and `b` also resolves `react@19.0.0`

### Additional information

While debugging and after reading [the changelog for 9.5.0](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v9.5.0), I decided to set `dedupe-peer-dependents=false` in `.npmrc`, kind of on a whim. This actually fixes the issue, but **I am confused, because we are not dealing with packages that are peer dependents**. 

It also seems odd to me that `react@19.0.0` would be able to deduplicate `react@18.3.0`, since the major versions differ.

Please let me know if there is any other information I can provide; I might have missed something 😌 

### Node.js version

v22.12.0

### Operating System

macOS

comments.body:
After some investigation, this seems to be an issue with `update --latest` and `dedupe-peer-dependents=true`, rather than `update` more generally.

For example, using an `@latest` specifier works as intended:

```shell
pnpm --filter a update react@latest
```

It updates only `packages/a/package.json`, and the relevant importers for `packages/a` in the lockfile:

```diff
diff --git a/packages/a/package.json b/packages/a/package.json
index 1ed69e4..96bf809 100644
--- a/packages/a/package.json
+++ b/packages/a/package.json
@@ -2,7 +2,6 @@
   "name": "a",
   "version": "1.0.0",
   "description": "",
   "main": "index.js",
   "scripts": {
     "test": "echo \"Error: no test specified\" && exit 1"
@@ -11,6 +10,6 @@
   "author": "",
   "license": "ISC",
   "dependencies": {
-    "react": "^18.2.0"
+    "react": "^19.0.0"
   }
 }
diff --git a/pnpm-lock.yaml b/pnpm-lock.yaml
index b56350f..43e002d 100644
--- a/pnpm-lock.yaml
+++ b/pnpm-lock.yaml
@@ -11,8 +11,8 @@ importers:
   packages/a:
     dependencies:
       react:
-        specifier: ^18.2.0
-        version: 18.2.0
+        specifier: ^19.0.0
+        version: 19.0.0
 
   packages/b:
     dependencies:
@@ -47,6 +47,10 @@ packages:
     resolution: {integrity: sha512-/3IjMdb2L9QbBdWiW5e3P2/npwMBaU9mHCSCUzNln0ZCYbcfTsGbTJrU/kGemdH2IWmB2ioZ+zkxtmq6g09fGQ==}
     engines: {node: '>=0.10.0'}
 
+  react@19.0.0:
+    resolution: {integrity: sha512-V8AVnmPIICiWpGfm6GLzCR/W5FXLchHop40W4nXBmdlEceh16rCN8O8LNWm5bh5XUX91fh7KpA+W0TgMKmgTpQ==}
+    engines: {node: '>=0.10.0'}
+
 snapshots:
 
   js-tokens@4.0.0: {}
@@ -65,3 +69,5 @@ snapshots:
   react@18.2.0:
     dependencies:
       loose-envify: 1.4.0
+
+  react@19.0.0: {}
```

On the other hand `--latest` seems to act like a "global" flag in this scenario, that gets threaded to the general `opts` for install and eventually to resolution: https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/512465c4ce0aeaf733c1fb08ccbd3731ad46ba35/pkg-manager/resolve-dependencies/src/index.ts#L133-L142.

The interaction with `dedupe-peer-dependents` seems incidental, and does not have to do with the deduping per se. Early on, [`opts.dedupePeerDependents` prompts a codepath that will do an install for all projects](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/512465c4ce0aeaf733c1fb08ccbd3731ad46ba35/pkg-manager/plugin-commands-installation/src/installDeps.ts#L204-L207), and thus `--latest` will end up doing a latest-version resolution for **every** package for the workspace 😱 

This means that other packages, aside from the specified one, will be updated. I updated the reproduction to show this issue, showing that a third workspace package with `is-negative` also gets updated: https://github.com/fpapado/pnpm-filtered-updated-changes-other-packages

@zkochan, this seems like a bit of a footgun, or at least inconsistent since `update --filter --latest` works with `dedupe-peer-dependents=false`. I have written some tests for this (need to clean up my branch), but fixing this might require some internal refactoring with how `--latest` gets treated. Another option would be to disallow `--latest` in this scenario. Have you run into similar cases before? How would you approach this?

referenced_prs.title: fix: `pnpm update --filter --latest` should only change relevant packages and projects, with `dedupe-peer-dependents=true`
referenced_prs.body:
This PR is an attempt to fix (or at least add tests for) https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/8877, based on the investigation described in this comment https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/8877#issuecomment-2559347513.

In short, it seems that with `dedupe-peer-dependents=true`, we end up running an installation on all workspace projects (which sounds correct, since we need that information to deduplicate). However, since `latest` is an option of the installation/resolution itself, we end up passing it forward/carrying it out for all projects and importers.

Conversely, this does not happen for the `dedupe-peer-dependents=false` codepath, since only the selected projects graph is passed to resolution. In other words, there is already a scenario where `--latest` acts "locally" for `pnpm update --filter`, which is a bit confusing.

This PR takes the approach of making "update to latest" a property to projects/importers, as `{updateToLatest?: boolean}`, instead of a property of the resolution. I followed some of the ideas in https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/6178, which was fixing a similar conceptual issue.

The tests seemed happy locally, but there is some flakiness that makes be a bit uncertain (aside: do you also have this issue with local tests?). I suggest we let the CI run and see what happens 🧪 I might have missed scenarios where `--latest` is used, and this change might not make sense in general 😅 

Let me know if you have any thoughts and I will adjust this PR accordingly, after some rest. Happy holidays!

issues.issue_title: properties.path() not working for dot-separated keys after upgrade from 2.1.1 to 2.2.0
issues.body:
Hi, thanks for this library! I'm using it to parse Spring-like properties files.

Given a properties file with no header and a dot-separated value:
```
testkey.nested=testval
```

In 2.1.1 I used to be able to do:
```
const propertiesReader = require("properties-reader");
const properties = propertiesReader("test.properties");
properties.path()
```
This would give an object: `{ testkey: { nested: 'testval' } }`

In 2.2.0, `path()` here returns: `{}`

issues.issue_title: jQuery 3.4.0+ silences native focus handlers attached after jQuery ones
issues.body:
<!--
Feature Requests:
  Please read https://github.com/jquery/jquery/wiki/Adding-new-features
  Most features should start as plugins outside of jQuery.

Bug Reports:
  Note that we only can fix bugs in the latest version of jQuery.
  Briefly describe the issue you've encountered
  *  What do you expect to happen?
  *  What actually happens?
  *  Which browsers are affected?
  Provide a *minimal* test case, see https://webkit.org/test-case-reduction/
  Use the latest shipping version of jQuery in your test case!
  We prefer test cases on JS Bin (https://jsbin.com/qawicop/edit?html,css,js,output) or CodePen (https://codepen.io/mgol/pen/wNWJbZ)

Frequently Reported Issues:
  * Self-closing tags broken in jQuery 3.5.0 or newer: please read the [jQuery 3.5.0 blog post](https://blog.jquery.com/2020/04/10/jquery-3-5-0-released/) & the [upgrade guide](https://jquery.com/upgrade-guide/3.5/); see also issue #4681.
-->

### Description ###

This may be related to the dicussion/resolution for #4856, but is a distinct issue.

If you have a Google Address autocomplete input, and trigger focus programatically (e.g. `$('input').trigger('focus')`) the autocomplete works fine. However, if you add any other focus event listener (event just an empty function, like `$('input').on('focus', function() {})`) then the autocomplete won't work until manually focused (e.g. through clicking or tabbing).


### Link to test case ###

Test case is at https://jsfiddle.net/bgmrujdt/1/. First autocomplete has a focus event handler, focusing by clicking the button does not work. Second autocomplete doesn't have a focus event handler, focusing by clicking the button does work. 

The same code with jQuery 3.3.1 works fine (example at https://jsfiddle.net/bgmrujdt/2/). It also works fine using native javascript `.focus()` instead of jQuery (https://jsfiddle.net/s2zmhb9t/)

comments.body:
Thanks for the report and the test case! Looks like a real issue that we should investigate along other focus-related issues.

I'm going to tentatively set the milestone to 3.6.1 mostly so that we look at it before the release but it's not guaranteed to be fixed there, especially as we still need to discover the cause.
BTW, since the `click` event uses `leverageNative`, it suffers from the same issues: https://jsbin.com/katowor/1/edit?html,js,console,output
PR: https://github.com/jquery/jquery/pull/5228

referenced_commits.message:
Event: Make trigger(focus/blur/click) work with native handlers

In `leverageNative`, instead of calling `event.stopImmediatePropagation()`
which would abort both native & jQuery handlers, set the wrapper's
`isImmediatePropagationStopped` property to a function returning `true`.
Since for each element + type pair jQuery attaches only one native handler,
there is also only one wrapper jQuery event so this achieves the goal:
on the target element jQuery handlers don't fire but native ones do.

Unfortunately, this workaround doesn't work for handlers on ancestors
- since the native event is re-wrapped by a jQuery one on each level of
the propagation, the only way to stop it for jQuery was to stop it for
everyone via native `stopPropagation()`. This is not a problem for
`focus`/`blur` which don't bubble, but it does also stop `click` on
checkboxes and radios. We accept this limitation.

Fixes gh-5015
Closes gh-5228

issues.issue_title: 1.3.26 broke auth with existing API keys

comments.body:
<!-- Answer -->
This regression with API keys breaking after upgrading to 1.3.26/1.3.27 is confirmed and tracked in [issue #4080](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/issues/4080). The root cause is a change in how the API key plugin validates the `x-api-key` header and session retrieval logic, which started in 1.3.7 and persists in later versions, resulting in 401 Unauthorized errors for previously valid keys.

A recent fix was merged ([PR #5317](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/5317)) that updates the authorization logic for API key handling, aligning it with the logic used for creating API keys. This should resolve flawed checks that caused the regression. If you are still seeing issues in 1.3.27, keep an eye out for the next release or try the 1.4 beta when available.

As a workaround, if you’re using API keys in a backend route (especially with frameworks like SvelteKit or Next.js), make sure to manually wrap the returned session object in a `Response` and ensure all error branches do the same. This helps avoid silent failures and ensures proper error handling until the fix is released.

For debugging, check the `errorWithStack` property in the `APIError` object for more details on authentication failures.

Let me know if you need help with workaround code or want to test the fix in a specific release.

issues.issue_title: Invalid typing using additionalFields

comments.body:
<!-- Greeting -->
Hi @simohammadi! I'm [Dosu](https://go.dosu.dev/dosubot) and I’m helping the better-auth team.

<!-- Answer -->
This is a known limitation in Better Auth 1.3.26 and later: full type inference for additionalFields (like your optional timeZone field) is not yet supported, which can result in incorrect or overly restrictive types in generated input types such as SignUpInput. This change was introduced in recent updates to the type inference logic for additionalFields, and the documentation now includes a warning about this limitation—improved type support is planned for the future [[source]](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/5146).

Currently, there is no official workaround for automatic type inference. The best approach is to manually augment or override the inferred types in your codebase where needed, for example by explicitly defining the expected input types for your forms or API calls. Keep an eye on future releases for improved support.

@dosu 

Dont think this is a valid answer. The types should not make me as a consumer of the apis have to typecast my inputs into the exact type of what is being inferred.

At least better auth could allow me as a user pass in anything from the typing standpoint, that is a better way of relaxing type support, for whatever reason.

Is it expected that for every additional field I add I need to typecast the property to never | null | undefined?

<!-- Answer -->
No, it's not expected or intended that you should have to typecast every additional field to `never | null | undefined`. This is a known limitation in Better Auth 1.3.26 and later—full type inference for `additionalFields` isn't supported yet, and the types can end up overly restrictive or incorrect for custom fields. There isn't an official way to relax type support or override this behavior right now, and no configuration or utility type exists to globally allow more permissive typing for these fields. The only workaround is to manually augment or override the inferred types in your own code until improved support is released [[source]](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/5146).

Other users have run into the same issue, and the consensus is that manual workarounds are necessary for now. If you want to avoid type errors, you can loosen your consumer-side type expectations (for example, using `any` or declaration merging), but this isn't ideal and should be temporary until the type system is improved.

issues.issue_title: Jest v30 compatibility issue with synckit@0.11.10 due to @pkgr/core dependency update
issues.body:
## Bug Report

### Summary
synckit@0.11.10 (released July 18, 2025) introduced a breaking change that causes Jest v30 tests to fail with a `createRequire` TypeError. This is due to updating the @pkgr/core dependency to a version incompatible with Jest's module loading.

### Error Message
```
TypeError: The argument 'filename' must be a file URL object, file URL string, or absolute path string. Received 'http://localhost/index.cjs'
    at Function.createRequire (node_modules/jest-runtime/build/index.js:1407:23)
    at Object.<anonymous> (node_modules/@pkgr/core/lib/index.cjs:10:48)
    at Object.<anonymous> (node_modules/synckit/lib/index.cjs:30:29)
    at _jestSnapshot (node_modules/@jest/expect/build/index.js:29:16)
    at createJestExpected (node_modules/@jest/expect/build/index.js:44:28)
    at node_modules/@jest/expect/build/index.js:52:41
    at node_modules/@jest/expect/build/index.js:53:3
    at Object.<anonymous> (node_modules/@jest/expect/build/index.js:56:12)
```

### Environment
- **synckit version**: 0.11.10 (broken), 0.11.9 (works)
- **Jest version**: 30.0.2+
- **@pkgr/core version**: 0.3.4 (broken), 0.2.9 (works)
- **Node.js version**: Latest
- **Package manager**: Any (affects pnpm, npm, yarn)

### Root Cause Analysis
1. **June 1, 2025**: `@pkgr/core@0.3.0` introduced breaking changes with Jest's `createRequire` implementation
2. **July 18, 2025**: `synckit@0.11.10` updated its dependency range to allow `@pkgr/core@0.3.x`, pulling in the incompatible version
3. **Dependency chain**: Jest v30 → @jest/expect → jest-snapshot → synckit → @pkgr/core

### Reproduction Repository
I've created a complete reproduction case: **https://github.com/FrozenPandaz/jest-synckit-issue**

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Clone the reproduction repository
2. Remove the pnpm override from `package.json` 
3. Delete `pnpm-lock.yaml` and run `pnpm install`
4. Run either:
   - `nx test test` (NX command)
   - `cd apps/test && TS_NODE_COMPILER_OPTIONS='{"moduleResolution":"node10","module":"commonjs","customConditions":null}' npx jest` (Jest directly)

Both will fail with the createRequire error above.

### Expected Behavior
Tests should run successfully as they did with synckit@0.11.9

### Actual Behavior
Jest tests fail to start due to module loading errors in the synckit → @pkgr/core dependency chain

### Current Workaround
Pin synckit to the last working version using package manager overrides:

**For pnpm:**
```json
{
  "pnpm": {
    "overrides": {
      "synckit": "0.11.8"
    }
  }
}
```

**For npm:**
```json
{
  "overrides": {
    "synckit": "0.11.8"
  }
}
```

**For yarn:**
```json
{
  "resolutions": {
    "synckit": "0.11.8"
  }
}
```

### Suggested Fix
Update synckit's dependency on @pkgr/core to exclude the problematic 0.3.x versions until they resolve Jest compatibility. For example:
- Pin to `@pkgr/core: "^0.2.0"` 
- Or exclude broken versions: `@pkgr/core: "^0.3.0 \!=0.3.0 \!=0.3.1 \!=0.3.2 \!=0.3.3 \!=0.3.4"`

### Impact
- Affects all Jest v30 users who depend on packages using synckit
- Common in NX projects, ESLint configurations, and other tooling
- Breaking change appeared suddenly on July 18, 2025 with synckit@0.11.10 release

### Additional Context
- This only surfaced yesterday due to synckit@0.11.10 updating its dependency range
- @pkgr/core versions 0.3.0+ are incompatible with Jest v30's createRequire implementation
- The issue occurs in Jest's core initialization, not user configuration
- No Jest configuration workaround exists that avoids this dependency chain

### Related Issues
- Similar createRequire issues in Jest: https://github.com/jestjs/jest/issues/9426
- This affects any test runner using similar module loading patterns

Thank you for maintaining synckit\! This library is widely used and this compatibility fix would help many Jest v30 users.

issues.issue_title: SSR strict host validation breaks application on cloud platform
issues.body:
### Command

other

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

21.1.4

### Description

My SSR application runs in a Kubernetes cluster, and behind a load balancer. After updating `@angular/ssr` to version 21.1.5, which contains the SSRF fix #32516, I am getting the following error logged server-side for every request:

```
URL with hostname "10.x.x.x" is not allowed.Please provide a list of allowed hosts in the "allowedHosts" option in the "CommonEngine" constructor.
Falling back to client side rendering. This will become a 400 Bad Request in a future major version.
```
The address `10.x.x.x` varies from one request to the next, because Kubernetes spins up multiple containers, each with a different private address.

I assume that either the load balancer or Kubernetes itself (not sure which) is passing the real hostname as `x-forwarded-host: my.real.hostname`, while setting `host: 10.x.x.x` on the internal request, where `10.x.x.x` is the dynamic internal IP request of each container instance.

I cannot resolve this with the `allowedHosts` option (or the `NG_ALLOWED_HOSTS` environment variable), because this option only supports either exact hostnames or a wildcard prefix such as `*.domain`. It does not support a wildcard _postfix_ such as `10.*`. I can't even hack a fix by using just `*`, as this also fails to match.

I can think of two possible solutions, each very different:

1. Extend the `allowedHosts` option to support glob-style wildcards. Then I could set `allowedHosts` to `['10.*', 'my.real.hostname']` (allowing for both headers).
2. If the later code that this validation is protecting always derives the real hostname as `x-forwarded-host || host` (pseudocode), then this SSRF protection should only need to validate the `host` header if `x-forwarded-host` is not present. Then I could set `allowedHosts` to just `['my.real.hostname']` and the private IP address in `host` wouldn't matter.

### Minimal Reproduction

- Create a new application with the latest versions, with `@angular/ssr` at version 21.1.5 or 21.2.0, and SSR enabled.
- Add at least one `RenderMode.Server` page in the server routes.
- Running the compiled module locally with Node.js, verify that the `URL with hostname "localhost" is not allowed` error occurs, but can be resolved by setting `NG_ALLOWED_HOSTS=localhost`, and that the SSR route is now server-side rendered.
- Build the compiled app into a Node.js container image.
- Deploy the container to a cloud service and give it a public hostname, but in such a way that traffic will be routed internally using a private IP address as the `host` header. (It may also be possible to reproduce running a Kubernetes cluster locally without a load balancer. I haven't verified this.)
- Access the SSR route, and observe that the page is not server-side rendered, and the `URL with hostname "10.x.x.x" is not allowed` error (or equivalent IP address) is logged out by the container.
- Try setting the `NG_ALLOWED_HOSTS` environment variable on the container, and observe that it is not possible to find a value that successfully resolves the error, except supplying the public hostname and the exact private IP address – until it changes. Any other value you try using a wildcard results in a 400 error.

I can try to create a simple example repo if necessary, but I hope this explanation is enough, together with inspecting the code change introduced in #32516.

### Exception or Error

```text
URL with hostname "10.x.x.x" is not allowed.Please provide a list of allowed hosts in the "allowedHosts" option in the "CommonEngine" constructor.
Falling back to client side rendering. This will become a 400 Bad Request in a future major version.
```

### Your Environment

```text
┌───────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────────┐
│ Package                           │ Installed Version │ Requested Version │
├───────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────────────┤
│ @angular-devkit/build-angular     │ 21.1.5            │ 21.1.5            │
│ @angular-devkit/core              │ 21.1.5            │ 21.1.5            │
│ @angular-devkit/schematics        │ 21.1.5            │ 21.1.5            │
│ @angular/animations               │ 21.1.6            │ 21.1.6            │
│ @angular/build                    │ 21.1.5            │ 21.1.5            │
│ @angular/cdk                      │ 21.1.6            │ 21.1.6            │
│ @angular/cli                      │ 21.1.5            │ 21.1.5            │
│ @angular/common                   │ 21.1.6            │ 21.1.6            │
│ @angular/compiler                 │ 21.1.6            │ 21.1.6            │
│ @angular/compiler-cli             │ 21.1.6            │ 21.1.6            │
│ @angular/core                     │ 21.1.6            │ 21.1.6            │
│ @angular/forms                    │ 21.1.6            │ 21.1.6            │
│ @angular/language-service         │ 21.1.6            │ 21.1.6            │
│ @angular/localize                 │ 21.1.6            │ 21.1.6            │
│ @angular/material                 │ 21.1.6            │ 21.1.6            │
│ @angular/platform-browser         │ 21.1.6            │ 21.1.6            │
│ @angular/platform-browser-dynamic │ 21.1.6            │ 21.1.6            │
│ @angular/platform-server          │ 21.1.6            │ 21.1.6            │
│ @angular/router                   │ 21.1.6            │ 21.1.6            │
│ @angular/ssr                      │ 21.1.5            │ 21.1.5            │
│ @schematics/angular               │ 21.1.5            │ 21.1.5            │
│ rxjs                              │ 7.8.2             │ 7.8.2             │

│ zone.js                           │ 0.16.0            │ 0.16.0            │
└───────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────┴───────────────────┘
```

### Anything else relevant?

I am using Google Kubernetes Engine behind Google Load Balancer, but other platforms may also show the issue. (I'm not certain whether it's the Load Balancer or Kubernetes that is using the IP address as the `host` header; possibly the latter, in which case it might be possible to reproduce the issue running Kubernetes locally.)

comments.body:
Since you are using `CommonEngine` you need to use `X-FOWARDED-HOST` yourself to build the proper URL in the `server.ts` middleware that the `render` method is invoked.

IE: replace `headers.host` with `headers[“X-FOWARDED-HOST"] || headers.host`, alternatively you could replace the `host` header with the `X-FOWARDED-HOST` in a previous middleware.

As a side note, `RenderMode.X` isn’t supported in the legacy `CommonEngine` API.

> IE: replace `headers.host` with `headers[“X-FOWARDED-HOST"] || headers.host`

@alan-agius4  Thank you - that resolves it. In that case, the new SSRF check must be working with a 'host' derived from the `CommonEngine` `url` property, rather than the original raw `host` header - which I didn't expect at all. There's perhaps a bit of a gap in the docs there – but that's understandable for an urgent fix. I appreciate your quick response.

> As a side note, RenderMode.X isn’t supported in the legacy CommonEngine API.

That's interesting, as it is still working and I don't see any deprecation warnings around `CommonEngine`. I will read up what I can on that. Thanks for the alert.

`CommonEngine` is not yet deprecated, but new functionality is only added to the modern APIs.  In your case it's looks like it is working because the `RenderMode` is `server`. But the `CommonEngine` itself doesn't use the server routes configuration at all.

Actually I found a case where a glob-style wildcard would still be useful.

I was using a server-side rendered page as my Kubernetes health-check URL. Because the cluster runs the health-check internally, it only sets `host: 10.x.x.x`, and no `x-forwarded-host`. Because of this, I've had to change my health-check to use a hard-coded response directly from `server.ts`, instead of being an SSR page. It's still a useful health-check, but it is now testing less of the stack. Being able to set `NG_ALLOWED_HOSTS` to include `10.*` would have been a useful solution.

Just some updates

It looks like two issues need to be solved:
- The first one is those `No such file:` lines, which are invalid symlinks in the framework itself. Maybe we can use `xattr -crs` instead.
- The second one is those frameworks and dylibs inside the framework. They all need to be signed as well. (https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/issues/8075)

@pewsheen  I previously had no trouble with building, code-signing and notarizing builds with 1.4. I was thinking of making a fake xattr and dropping it into the build path so I can upgrade to Tauri 1.5 before Apple cuts off my use of atool for notarizing.

Might be worth trying `xattr -crs` as you suggested, or use a find and pipe the results to xattr, e.g. `find /path/to/base_directory -type f -exec xattr -c {} \;`

Are you bundling Accelerate.framework with the app bundle? (`/Users/me/projects/accelerate_test/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/macos/accelerate_test.app/Contents/Frameworks/Accelerate.framework`). I might be missing something, but why do you have to do that? Isn't that framework included with macOS?

Tip to anyone coming across this: Make sure that your version of `xattr` supports the `-r` option. My Python Poetry installation was overriding the system `xattr` binary on my $PATH. Run `which xattr` -- it should return `/usr/bin/xattr`. If it returns something else, remove whatever it is from your $PATH and try again.

issues.issue_title: Query string array parsing behavior changed in version 6.14.1

comments.body: It was introduced as a CVE fix - meaning, your current setup should not have worked in the first place, and on v6.14.0 your application is vulnerable. If you want up to 50, then pass the arrayLimit option set to 50 in the `parse` call, and stick with v6.14.1.
Hi @ljharb. Thank you very much for your clarification and your time.

I don't think an env var makes much sense, and if something is using qs transitively and not providing you with a means to configure it, then that's something you should file an issue on the intervening project about.

The decision of setting `arrayLimit` to `20` by default is absolutely a breaking change.

If it was set to 25, it wouldn't have been a breaking change for us. But maybe for someone else it would have been.

If this was the solution for DOS attacks, why go as low as 20? There are many nodejs apps that use query params for 25/50/100 items per page.

The issue isn't the specific number - it's that this was a _vulnerability_. The array limit was always meant to protect you here.

20 is the existing default, and it probably was pretty arbitrary when first selected.

To be clear: "this version broke something for me" is NOT the same as "this version is a breaking change". This is not a breaking change; it's a bug fix. If something broke, it was because you were incorrectly relying on the lack of arrayLimit protection.

So i investigated this [vulnerability](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6rw7-vpxm-498p) and it seems like it might not cause a DoS at all.

If you get qs 6.14.0 and run slightly modified (added qs version) POC code from there:

```js
const qs = require('qs');

console.log('qs version:', require('qs/package.json').version);
console.log('');

const attack = 'a[]=' + Array(10000).fill('x').join('&a[]=');
const result = qs.parse(attack, { arrayLimit: 100 });
console.log(result.a.length);  // Output: 10000 (should be max 100)
```

it outputs:

```sh
code/test-qs-dos $ node poc.js
qs version: 6.14.0

1000
```

So `arrayLimit` is bypassed, yes. But `parameterLimit` still kicks in and prevents array from growing to 10000.

Am i missing something?

So if above is correct then arrayLimit fix can be declared as breaking change and reverted. Then patched in 7.x as your point below is no longer valid

> If I agreed it was a breaking change, then I would be compelled to revert it, and publish a new major, and **tons of people on v6 would be left vulnerable**. ([source](https://github.com/ljharb/qs/pull/538#discussion_r2662264456))

Additionally for unindexed arrays like `a[]=1&a[]=2&...&a[]=10000` with applied arrayLimit resulting object would use similar (or slightly more) memory as array, so even without `parameterLimit` enabling `arrayLimit` for unindexed arrays does nothing as protection against DoS. That;s probably why it wasn't implemented back then

Just because a single query doesn't cause a DOS, doesn't mean it's not one. The capability exists, which means that a) one request can create multiple of these large arrays, and b) multiple calls to `parse` (think, "requests to a webserver") can build up memory pressure, causing a DOS.

`arrayLimit` was introduced to prevent memory exhaustion using indexed array. When parsing query strings like `a[999999999]=b`, the parser would need to create an array with 1 billion empty slots before setting the value at index 999999999. This causes: 1. Memory exhaustion - allocating huge sparse arrays 2. CPU exhaustion - iterating over massive arrays
```
a[999999999] = 'b'
// JavaScript allocates array with length 1,000,000,000
// Memory: ~4-8GB just for the array structure (even though mostly empty)
```
Returning `{'a': '999999999'}` object in this case prevents allocation of huge array 

With unindexed array it's not possible to create array bigger than 1000 elements (because of parameter limit). 
So for your point **a**: array with 1000 elements is not a problem for javascript (i wouldn't even call it large). 
For point **b**: returning object with 1000 keys instead of array with 1000 elements does not ease memory pressure (correct me if i am wrong)

> I don't think an env var makes much sense, and if something is using qs transitively and not providing you with a means to configure it, then that's something you should file an issue on the intervening project about.

The logic is correct, but the logistics become an issue for thousands of third-party packages that must follow. It is fair to say that qs is a fundamental block, and sane, high defaults would be much more welcome. The negative impact would be negligible, whereas this has the potential for a high negative impact.
Based on @kroleg 's comments I think is valid to reopen the issue and continue the discussion here. Thank you all.
created separate issue to discuss vulnerability which triggered this change https://github.com/ljharb/qs/issues/539
@MichalKolekMG the negative impact of higher limits is MUCH larger than the negative impact of a few tests failing in applications that have lockfiles.

1. This `arrayLimit=20` is there since `qs` was forked from `querystring` (which happened in 2014), nobody knows why it's 20. It never bothered anyone because nobody (or very few) was affected until this fix.

2. With default value `paramLimit` of 1000 i don't see how enforcing `arrayLimit` for **unindexed** arrays does anything for DoS protection.
  - with `arrayLimit=20` i can pass 50 arrays of 20 items
  - without `arrayLimit` i can pass 1 array of 1000 items
  these will consume same amount of memory. I think 50 array will consume more because of array management overhead (headers and etc)

3. For indexed array it makes sense to enforce `arrayLimit` ([see above](#issuecomment-3717668186))

imo more consistent solution of DoS would be: if unindexed -> always array, for indexed -> always object. This will also allow to get rid of this magic number `20` and `arrayLimit`

For me this change completely broke one of the express endpoints of my server, because the array was getting converted to an object, thus removing all array functions from it. This shouldn't be a minor. 

Just to clarify, I was straight up using the value returned from express. (and it also just happened when it exceeded the limit)
We suffer the same problem, because in a legacy project we are dependent on Loopback which has QS as a transient dependency...

IMO @ljharb was acting out of best intentions trying to fix severe vulnerability. That's why this fix with breaking change was introduced in patch (see [comment](https://github.com/ljharb/qs/pull/538#discussion_r2662264456)).

But it turned out this vulnerability is not severe https://github.com/ljharb/qs/issues/539
So IMO right thing to do now would be to admit that this was a breaking change which should have been released in major version bump and revert it.
It still remains a bug and a vulnerability even if not a severe one, and I can guarantee you I will not revert it.
Bug? yes. Vulnerability? Nope
Being a bug means it's not a breaking change, and won't be reverted.

Bug and breaking change are not mutually exclusive.

You've made a mistake and just trying to save face. That's it

The mistake was assuming that something would always be an array, when the library doesn't guarantee that.

Making personal accusations is a CoC violation; please self-moderate.
Your Readme states that it parses arrays if you use the [] notation, so anyone would expect it does so without any other conditions of the stated in there previously. It is a breaking change.
@jaume-perez if you read farther, it talks about arrayLimit, so you could never safely assume that you'll always get an array.

> Being a bug means it's not a breaking change

Respectfully disagree. You can absolutely push a bug fix out, that is great to do. But if it _breaks existing functionality_ than it is, _by definition_ a _breaking change_. The two are not mutually exclusive. This is probably a great thing to fix, it just need to be a major version change so that people can apply it accordingly.
@DylanPittman the broken behavior - the bug itself - is existing functionality. (see https://xkcd.com/1172/). Every bug fix is a potential breaking change - it's not cut and dry.

The analysis in this thread and in #539 - particularly from @kroleg demonstrating the parameterLimit interaction, and from @krzysdz providing the thorough historical  context - has been valuable in accurately assessing the severity of GHSA-6rw7-vpxm-498p. I've updated the advisory severity from High to Low, since the default  `parameterLimit` of `1000` effectively prevents the DoS scenario described in the original report.

The fix in 6.14.1 remains correct: `arrayLimit` is a documented option that should apply consistently across all array notations, and this was a bug. Additionally, the  investigation here surfaced a more meaningful issue: comma-separated values (when `comma: true` is set) were not subject to `arrayLimit` at all and could bypass `parameterLimit` entirely. This will be fixed shortly and will ship in the next patch release.

For anyone affected by the 6.14.1 change: if your application needs arrays larger than the default `arrayLimit` of 20, pass `arrayLimit` explicitly in your `qs.parse()` call (e.g., `{ arrayLimit: 50 }`). If you consume qs transitively through a framework that doesn't expose this configuration, please file an issue on that framework to do so.

comments.body:
I forced rollup@3.10.0 using yarn's selective dependency resolution but that didn't fix it either.

@patak-dev Do you have more experience with this?

I investigated further and checked the heap allocation of `vite build` using Clinic Doctor. Looks like a terrible performance issue since 4.2.0, the heap used simply doubled. Vite 4.1.5: Vite 4.3.9 (tested with 4.2.0 as well, graph looks similar) As mentioned before I forced yarn to use rollup 3.10.0, which was the version Vite used before 4.2.0, but I don't see any difference. I'm assuming there's a significant performance issue introduced in Vite 4.2.0.

Update: Just to be clear, the out-of-memory issue is because my CI environment does not have much memory. The question is why Vite 4.2.0 uses much more memory than before.

Did some more tests and ran the heap profiler with and without `--sourcemap false` with version `4.1.5` and `4.3.9`.

| --sourcemap | Vite 4.1.5   | Vite 4.3.9 |
|--------------:|-----------:|----------:|
| true                 | 3,300 MB | 3,300 MB |
| false                | 1,750 MB  | 3,300 MB |

I'm not sure why, but I'm getting different results when building without sourcemaps on 4.3.9. Either the graph looks exactly as if I'm building with sourcemaps (3,300 MB), but sometimes it lowers to 2,500 MB. (Edit: I've run the build command many times now, and now it's always 3,300 MB like the screenshot above. Maybe some unexpected optimization happened that caused it to drop for a while?)

Either way, I guess something has changed related to sourcemaps, as the results with are nearly identical.

@bluwy Found the issue finally. [This commit](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/commit/ee3b90a812e863fc92f485ce53a4e764a2c34708) broke the CLI option `--sourcemap false`, as it converts `false` to a string. This can be checked when running `vite build --debug --sourcemap false`, you will see it still outputs sourcemaps.

Thanks for figuring this out @dd-jonas (and sorry for the breakage). Didn't expect this to happen and feels like a weird behaviour from cac, it wants us to [support `--no-sourcemap` instead](https://github.com/cacjs/cac#negated-options), but I don't think that's ideal.

Would you like to send a PR fixing this? The changes should be here:

https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/92e5c5df22cdb37e17d39660a1c1d6e96ec81855/packages/vite/src/node/cli.ts#L73-L91

Handling the `"false"` as `false` instead. Or I can tackle this tomorrow too.

---

You can also workaround this for now but setting the config at `build.sourcemap: false` instead in `vite.config.js`. (and remove the CLI arg)
@bluwy Cheers, I opened a PR here https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/13663. Feel free to suggest a different approach if you think there's a better way to tackle this.

issues.issue_title: Upgrading from v4.1.4 to v4.3.9 causes dev server to fail when prebundling CommonJS node packages
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

**Current Set Up**
- I have a React repo created with Vite 4.1.4
- I have another repo created by [Bit](https://bit.dev/). Essentially, they build my components using Webpack and allow exporting to their cloud servers. These components can then be imported like any `node_modules` packages
- While using Vite 4.1.4, everything works fine with this flow. I make a React component in Bit with CSS module, export it to cloud, then import it in my Vite repo. Both dev server and build shows everything is working as expected and has been running fine for about 3 months
- Yesterday, I saw a warning about a security issue and I should upgrade to Vite 4.3.9. I upgraded and the bug appears.

**Bug**
- Dev server would run without any errors. However, navigating to the page would show an empty screen. Checking the `console` yields the following errors:
  
![image](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/assets/43018778/7c31143d-2fd7-4fd0-857c-6f6dfa60801b)

- These errors never happened before. It comes from components that imports a CSS module like so:
  - `import classes from "./tooltip.module.css"`
- Before, the dev server would run fine and no such error would happened. There were warnings like below but the site would work without any issues:
- 
![image](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/assets/43018778/4f429050-0200-4683-ae2a-4af46d94f30e)

- Running `vite build` would yields a functional build with no issues.

**What I've Found/Tried**
- I thought it's a problem related to my CSS module -> tried to use my packages in a CRA project and everything works fine
- I thought it's a Bit problem -> my package works fine in a CRA project and in a Vite production build
- Googling and searching through the issues yields problems related to CommonJS, ESBuild, and Vite:
  - Several Issues related to Rollup's `plugin-commonjs`. However, since this happens during dev, it's likely to be a ESBuild problem.
  - [Monorepos and Linked Directories](https://vitejs.dev/guide/dep-pre-bundling.html#monorepos-and-linked-dependencies) -> I'm not using a monorepo since the packages are installed via `npm install`. I did try adding the `optimizeDeps` property with the `build.commonjsOptions` but nothing works:
  
```
{
  optimizeDeps: {
    include: ['@hellopocketed/react-ui.widgets.tooltip'],
  },
  build: {
    commonjsOptions: {
      include: ['@hellopocketed/react-ui.widgets.tooltip', /node_modules/, /@hellopocketed\/*/]
    }
  }
}
}
``` 
  - Adding various CommonJS plugins for `rollup` and `esbuild` also yields no results.

### Reproduction

https://drive.google.com/file/d/1OV5dgpYnel8jQI6ype5BNqfNSIMH2dlz/view?usp=sharing

### Steps to reproduce

Part 1
- Download and unzip the package.  The current Vite version is 4.1.4. No need to run `npm install`
- Navigate inside it and run `npm run dev`. There should be a warning regarding the stylesheet but the script would work.
- You should see a functional start page with a hoverable tooltip

Part 2
- Upgrade `vite` using `npm install vite@4.3.9`
  - If you run into trouble with the `@hellopocketed` package being not found, copy it out of the module and remove it from the `package.json`, then run `npm install` again. Once `vite` is updated, add the package and its entry back.
- Run `npm run dev` again and go to the site. The script should run with no warnings or errors.
- However, when you go to the site, it will be blank. Checking the console would show the errors.

### System Info

```shell
System:
    OS: Windows 10 10.0.19045
    CPU: (12) x64 Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-6800K CPU @ 3.40GHz   
    Memory: 18.47 GB / 31.90 GB
  Binaries:
    Node: 16.14.2 - C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.EXE
    npm: 8.5.0 - C:\Program Files\nodejs\npm.CMD
  Browsers:
    Edge: Spartan (44.19041.1266.0), Chromium (114.0.1823.37)
    Internet Explorer: 11.0.19041.1566
```


### Used Package Manager

npm

### Logs

_No response_

### Validations

- [X] Follow our [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [X] Read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [X] Read the [docs](https://vitejs.dev/guide).
- [X] Check that there isn't [already an issue](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues) that reports the same bug to avoid creating a duplicate.
- [X] Make sure this is a Vite issue and not a framework-specific issue. For example, if it's a Vue SFC related bug, it should likely be reported to [vuejs/core](https://github.com/vuejs/core) instead.
- [X] Check that this is a concrete bug. For Q&A open a [GitHub Discussion](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/discussions) or join our [Discord Chat Server](https://chat.vitejs.dev/).
- [X] The provided reproduction is a [minimal reproducible example](https://stackoverflow.com/help/minimal-reproducible-example) of the bug.

EDIT:
- I also tried to downgrade vite to `4.2x` but it still fails. Nothing jumps out at me when checking the `CHANGELOG.md` either but I'm not a pro at this so I could have missed something.
- Bit is just the mechanism for deploying packages. The packages themselves are React components written in Typescript and is compiled via Webpack to CommonJS format.

issues.issue_title: AOT compilation removes beforeHandle when using arrow function expression

comments.body:
It seems Node preserves minified code (from tsx), and this breaks because `Function.toString()` returns minified.

https://github.com/elysiajs/elysia/blob/218c12a7a396a6f32ad9c2042d889027ab2cb3b1/src/compose.ts#L396-L424

I've submitted a fix for this in #1623. 

The root cause was that `hasReturn` used hardcoded character positions assuming `) => expr` format, which fails when minified to `)=>expr`.

The fix uses `indexOf('=>')` to find the arrow operator regardless of spacing.

Oh wow, that's one of the weird quirk haha
Thank you for this one
For document, this will be published under 1.4.22 #1657

referenced_prs.title: Datepicker: Hide the UI on destroy
referenced_prs.body:
Issue: https://github.com/jquery/jquery-ui/issues/2178 - date picker remains after being destroyed

We confirmed through git bisect that this commit, https://github.com/jquery/jquery-ui/commit/817ce38,  introduced a bug while fixing a memory leak with the date picker. This commit sets the current instance to null, https://github.com/jquery/jquery-ui/blob/5665215a8560832193735d9507a90d10e03b90c8/ui/widgets/datepicker.js#L440, to remove the date picker logic but fails to remove the UI widget. 

Our proposed fix is to hide the date picker when the destroy function using `$.datepicker._hideDatepicker();` so the user can no longer hover over a "ghost" date picker that can no longer be interacted with.

@fnagel

The following text is the understanding we have of what happened. The date picker was getting destroyed, but a lingering reference to it was kept alive (curInst). This meant it was a memory leak. The PR that fixed the memory leak did not handle the case where the datepicker was already open. It clears curInst but it does not actually destroy or remove the DOM element

To answer your question about setting this.curInst to null; curInst is being set to null, but the datepicker still thinks it is open, so other parts of the code still access _curInst which is why we set this.curInst to null.

In order to directly address how we could get rid of the daterpicker UI that's still open, we get rid of the div instance by destroying it from the DOM and clearing dp div by setting it to null. 

Here are the screenshots with our fix for before and after the div instance is destroyed:
![Screenshot 2024-07-15 100202](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7c1516e4-1619-485b-9203-0e5977e33d75)
![Screenshot 2024-07-15 100147](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/302f9141-d9a8-47f3-b916-b56f164b6157)

Here is a screenshot of the stack trace:
![image (1)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ae300407-d14e-4d42-b2a4-9a098a7e5f99)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ea979573-7937-480f-ab70-dbda1888ada7)

> Here is a screenshot of the stack trace:

@DawnSovereign are you able to get this stack trace with the local, unminified code? or click on it and see what function it's in, and find the corresponding function in the source code? 

from the screenshot, it looks like it's this function, right?

https://github.com/jquery/jquery-ui/blob/5e4f1b86296c5a977abc7efaff671ea9004d4d37/ui/widgets/datepicker.js#L2166-L2177
You can also see that existing tests are not passing, please make sure they do.

@mgol  Thanks for taking a look. We've pushed a unit test that reproduces the issue. It fails in `main` and passes in this branch with the fix.

We've reverted the fix back to hiding the datepicker instead of destroying the div. This is because several tests expect to re-use the element after it is destroyed. If we want to properly remove the element when the datepicker is destroyed, it looks like this may be a breaking change? I can open a ticket for that separately with more details.

The underlying issue is that destroying the datepicker by itself does not hide it. The current tests in `main` don't show this problem because they always hide the datepicker first before destroying it. So it is possible for a user to work around this problem at the moment by hiding before destroying.

The long term solution is to remove the element when the datepicker is destroyed, and update the tests, and mark this as a (potential?) breaking change.

At first I thought that just hiding the elements instead of destroying sounds not ideal, but then I've seen the comment about "This is because several tests expect to re-use the element after it is destroyed." so the change makes sense to me. 

It's not ideal that the destroy method does not really destroy everything (elements, events, ...) like other widgets do, but the Datepicker does not use the widget factory and always was a little special. 

So to me, this change improves the current state and fixes a bug introduces with 1.13.x. Only the test comment is a little confusing (see my review).

@mgol We might want to squash the commits when merging this.

@fnagel Was the comment your only concern to address before merging? I get your comment about destroying; I had a look at the code and it seemed not that easy to retrofit it into the existing design. `_hideDatepicker` may use an animation and we'd have to destroy only when it's done, but it doesn't provide any hook to do so. We'd have to add one, then add tests, also fix existing tests to not depend on it existing... Maybe let's leave it as it is for now.

Please approve if you have no further concerns to address.

@mgol I'm fine with merging it as it is. Datepicker was always special (as mentioned before, no widget factory in use) and SHOULD have been replaced with the new calendar and datepicker widget but never has.

Not sure what little surprises will come up when we start changing how the structure and design currently looks ;-)

Just to make sure, I checked myself what was the cause of the original issue. Datepicker attaches a global `mousedown` on document:
https://github.com/jquery/jquery-ui/blob/cd41c45d917d18839ab800816070db09a359d5bf/ui/widgets/datepicker.js#L2201
It never removes it. This handler hides the datepicker in certain conditions - but the first thing it checks is whether `$.datepicker._curInst` is truthy:
https://github.com/jquery/jquery-ui/blob/cd41c45d917d18839ab800816070db09a359d5bf/ui/widgets/datepicker.js#L1005-L1022
Since #1852 made `_curInst` cleared, this method stopped doing anything.

Some parts of the description from #2178 are incorrect, though - in 1.12.1, the datepicker UI was _not hidden_ on destroy either! It was just hidden after the first `mousedown`. If you just hovered over the datepicker or clicked on any of its elements, you'd get lots of console errors even in 1.12.1.

Therefore, this PR actually changes the behavior compared to 1.12.1 which was already partially broken. I think it's a reasonable change - the datepicker UI should hide when destroying the widget - but let's call it out.

Is the npm command being run as root, or some other user?

I'd like to try to zoom in on the problem and leave the docker aspect out of it.

If I understand this correctly:

- The user running `npm install` is root
- The `$HOME` directory is `/root` or some other root owned directory
- Thus the cache folder in `$HOME/.npm` is root-owned.
- But pacote is executing a git command based on the user of the ultimate _target_ of the extraction, not the cwd where the git action is taking place, and it fails.

Simpler reproduction, sans docker:

When I previously post log for issue I investigated the problem.

This happens bacuase npm tries to clone (`git clone` subprocess) in temp directory for current user but it runs as current directory owner user where `npm` runs. 

In my case the owner of directory was `node` but I run npm as root user.  So npm start process as root-user (because I run it as root user), but when `git clone` supbrocess runs it tries clone in temp directory for root user as `node` user whose haven't enough rigth to create subdirectories during `git clone`.

To prevent this issue (untill it would be fixed) you must run `npm` command as user who is current directory owner, for example:
```
runuser -u node -- npm install
```

Or change owner for current directory:
```
chown $(whoami) .
```

I don't believe the main issue here is OS specific.  It is dependent on the version of npm installed, and the way in which it is installed.  It is possible that a _different_ issue is preventing a global npm install to a shared drive with a different underlying file system (like a Windows or Linux VM for example), but that is likely fixed by the update to `@npmcli/move-file` that was done in a recent npm v7 release.

Any time npm tries to install a global package, it stubbornly refuses to overwrite executables (and man pages) that do not belong to the package being installed.  "Belong" meaning "is a symbolic link (or windows shim) into the package folder."  This is a very important security feature, which also prevents plenty of non-malicious but very hazardous mistakes, so that a global install doesn't quietly overwrite things it shouldn't.

You can tell npm to overwrite files unsafely by specifying `--force` to remove recommended protections.  If Homebrew is installing npm somewhere other than the global location that npm manages, but links npm's executable/mans into the same location where npm puts files for global installs, then yes, you will always run into this with a Homebrew install when running `npm i -g npm`.

There are two solutions:

1. Install with `--force` the first time you update after a Homebrew install.
2. Install npm and Node.js using something other than Homebrew.

comments.body:
It looks like with Prisma v7 the sendVerificationOTP method defined in your emailOTP plugin isn’t being triggered, even though your verification.create.after hook is working properly and manually calling sendVerificationOTP as intended. This behavior suggests that the plugin’s injected call isn’t being executed—likely an issue with how the Prisma v7 adapter handles hook order or method invocation compared to Prisma v6. You might consider the following next steps:

• Verify you’re using the latest compatible version of our Prisma adapter for Prisma v7, as improvements or fixes may have been released.
• As a temporary workaround, continue to rely on your manual call from the verification.create.after hook to send your OTP emails.
• Double-check your adapter and plugin configuration to ensure no changes in Prisma v7 affect the lifecycle of your verification record or hook execution.

Hi @elecrenPLB! I'm [Dosu](https://go.dosu.dev/dosubot) and I’m helping the better-auth team.

<!-- Answer -->
The `sendVerificationOTP` function in the emailOTP plugin is only triggered by the plugin's own endpoint logic—not by database hooks or direct verification record creation. The typical flow is: the `/api/email-otp/send-verification-otp` endpoint creates a verification record, then (if the user exists, or sign-in is allowed for new users) calls your `sendVerificationOTP` callback. If the verification record creation fails, is aborted by a hook, or the user doesn't exist, the function is never called and the record may be deleted immediately ([plugin code reference](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/98803e1c5f4fe93d9e13ab5917ab8f688b132973/packages/better-auth/src/plugins/email-otp/index.ts#L223-L1223)).

With Prisma v7, there are known issues with schema mapping and config changes (like custom model names or CLI-generated schema mismatches) that can cause verification record creation to silently fail or abort, which prevents the plugin from firing its callback ([schema mapping issue](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/issues/4781), [Prisma v7 migration](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/issues/6277)). This is why your manual after-hook workaround works: it bypasses the plugin's endpoint logic and sends the OTP directly after the record is created.

To troubleshoot and fix:
- Make sure you're using the `/api/email-otp/send-verification-otp` endpoint (not just creating verification records directly).
- Double-check that your Better Auth config model and field names (especially for `verification`) exactly match your Prisma schema. Prisma v7 requires manual updates to the schema and config after CLI generation.
- Enable debug logging in your adapter to trace verification record creation and catch any silent errors.
- If you use custom model names, verify that the adapter is mapping them correctly to your Prisma schema.

Until Better Auth fully supports Prisma v7 schema/config changes, your manual after-hook workaround is a valid solution. If you want to track this for future fixes, see the [Prisma v7 compatibility issue](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/issues/6277).

I use the... `let response = await axios(apiConfig);` ... format and get a 400 Bad Request, in what appears to be a circular error in 0.21.2 - confirmed the same behavior also in 0.21.4 & 0.23.0 (didn't bother to check 0.22.x)

return to 0.21.1 with no app code change, and all works as expected

LONG log attached from the response - with sensitive info either dropped or replaced by `***removed***`
The attached log was generated by a single request to a single endpoint

Hope this helps.

[axios.21.2.error.log.txt](https://github.com/axios/axios/files/7421120/axios.21.2.error.log.txt)

@davidmcl Try to unset the `Content-Type` header for GET requests, since GET request can't have a body (but in your case, it is a string 'null').

```
2021-10-22T16:53:45.313348826Z     url: 'https://v3.recurly.com/***removed***',
2021-10-22T16:53:45.313371350Z     method: 'get',
```
