2021-10-22T16:53:45.313379037Z     headers: {
2021-10-22T16:53:45.313382375Z       Accept: 'application/vnd.recurly.v2019-10-10, application/pdf',
2021-10-22T16:53:45.313385863Z       Authorization: 'Basic ***removed***',
2021-10-22T16:53:45.313389328Z       'Content-Type': 'application/json', <<<<<<<???
2021-10-22T16:53:45.313392713Z       'User-Agent': 'axios/0.21.2',
2021-10-22T16:53:45.313396073Z       'Content-Length': 4
2021-10-22T16:53:45.313399380Z     },
```
@DigitalBrainJS we cant do that as the RFC says `A payload within a GET request message has no defined semantics` please see [RFC7231](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/inline-errata/rfc7231.html)

Sorry for the delayed response...and I don't really have a preference here, since I now understand the reason for the previous failure was that the `data` parameter should not have been specified for a `GET`, but just a thought...

Since, by definition: The value `null` represents the intentional absence of any object value.

Would it not be acceptable/consistent when `data` is passed as null, that there is no value passed for the body; and aren't you applying semantics when you do a `JSON.stringify` ?  :smile: 

Question... If a `null` was passed for `data` in an axios request using POST, PUT, etc., where `data` is a valid parameter -- would the payload be `null`, empty, or  `'null'` ?  _My_ preference would be option 1, option 2 would be OK, but option 3 is not what I would expect.

Cheers,
David

> Would it not be acceptable/consistent when data is passed as null

no, empty body is not a valid JSON payload, so JSON.parse('') will throw an exception

> would the payload be **null**, empty, or 'null' 

The first option confuses me. I wonder how you're going to transfer `null` javascript type through the plain-text protocol without serializing it to a string :) In any case, we're not TC39 and we don't maintain the RFC. If the Axios request is JSON, it follows the JSON RFC.

The other two cases `[empty]|"null"`depend on `content-type` header.
Both `null` & `undefined` passed as the payload will be treated as empty request payload (0 bytes), unless the `content-type` header is set to `application/json`. In this case JSON.stringify is used for non-undefined values:
`undefined` => not set ([empty body])
`null` => `"null"`
`string` => `"string"`
`number` => `String(number)`
`boolean`=> `String(boolean)`

issues.issue_title: [BUG] Tar is very slow on npm 6.14.15
issues.body:
# What / Why

npm 6.14.15 is horribly slow, and it seems to result from upgrading `tar` from 4.4.14 to 4.4.19.

To reproduce you can try and install a package that needs to extract data like geo-tz(6.0.1). On GHA we saw an increase in npm install from 1 minute to 7 minutes!!!

Check out this repo github actions timing: 
https://github.com/Tallyb/slow-npm/actions/runs/1228854056

comments.body: I can confirm that. However, its not the node version but NPM, 6.14.14 was fine 6.14.15 is not. The change of the `tar` version is from 4.4.15 to 4.4.19.

I've narrowed it down to 4.4.16. Tested with `material-design-icons` `3.0.1`.
NPM version: `6.14.14`

I manually changed the `tar` dependency in the npm package.json to `4.4.16`, then `npm i` (for npm). With that the processing time goes up from ~120 seconds to 300+ seconds.

Oh, just for future reference: I got here because my builds stopped working after the `node:lts-buster` image was upgraded last to use NPM 6.14.15. NPM would start timing out with "cb() never called".

I have the same problem. It seems related to the directory caching mechanism in mkdir: by disabling the cache, that can simply done by changing the functions `cGet` and `cSet` in `lib/mkdir.js` to empty functions, I improved installation time of geo-tz from 1.33 minutes to just 10s on Linux. It seems faster to try to make the directory, and fail because the file exist, than to write and lookup in the cache, when you have a lot of directories. On Windows it took ages (10s of minutes), with this simple fix only 46 seconds. 

I made other tests, and it seems that the cause is the function `pruneCache` that iterates on every item in the cache. By bypassing it the performance is even better but it should have implications. If I instead change the cache data structure from a Map to a Set the performance seems to improve significantly.
I have similar performance issues on 7.x and 8.x npm versions as well. npm install runs 3-4 times slowly than on 6.14.14 npm version.
For reference, this appears to be the issue where people noticed that something was going on with NPM: https://github.com/npm/cli/issues/3676

issues.confirmation_reasoning: Non-maintainer commenters independently reported the same significant slowdown after the tar upgrade (notably alerighi describing a reproduction and large timing improvement when altering mkdir caching). issues.issue_title: Regression in 0.7.0: Namespace prefixes being introduced unnecessarily
issues.body:
We are using xmldom to parse, tweak, and serialize some SVG schematics that will ultimately be embedded in HTML (not xhtml) pages. Through 0.6.0, everything was working fine, but starting with 0.7.0, for some but not all documents, when we SerializeToString(doc), all of the elements in the document get prefixed by the svg namespace (<xvg:g>, etc.) This produces SVG documents that are perfectly legitimate XML but won't display when embedded in HTML5 documents due to HTML rules, which don't include the general XML rules for namespaces. 

1. What causes xmldom to do this? We didn't discover an identifiable pattern. 
2. How can we ensure that we get SVG we can use?

Right now we're hacking the results as text to lop off the namespaces so our app will continue to work, but we really don't want to do that.

Update by @karfau:
The regression was introduced in #268

comments.body:
Thank you for reporting that.
Just from looking into the changelog for 0.7.0 I see that we fixed https://github.com/xmldom/xmldom/pull/268 which sounds like it could be related.

Can you provide a minimal example SVG that shows the issue, So I can compare the output.
Please also tell us the exact argument(s) you putting into `parseFromString` and `serializeToString`. (Have you tried to parse or serialize them as/to HTML instead of XML?)

That being said, I think our test coverage regarding SVG it quite minimal:
Here is our only test so far: 
https://github.com/xmldom/xmldom/blob/3b18dd525287c90163ec964ca537c98a304afbe2/test/parse/simple.test.js#L39-L53
And I don't see any namespaces in the snapshot: https://github.com/xmldom/xmldom/blob/a681852df13f6bbbfe4a4727b2b538cdf09b9d56/test/parse/__snapshots__/simple.test.js.snap#L19-L28

Would be nice to improve the coverage on this. If you feel like it you could also create a PR with a test (that passes when addign it to 0.6.0 and currently fails) and we will see what we can do about it.
Supplied failing test in https://github.com/xmldom/xmldom/pull/321

It's very interesting. I just checked the XML Namespaces docs regarding duplicate namespaces:
It is not allowed to declare the same namespace (url) with two different prefixes, but it's allowed to declare it as the default namespace and a prefixed namespace:
https://www.w3.org/TR/xml-names11/#uniqAttrs
There is of course nothing being said about which one has precedence in those cases.

I just checked that chrome is dealing with that case the way you are describing in your test (thanks a lot for this!).

I think we should also add tests for correct treatment of "overlapping namespaces" when they are overlapping on different levels:
- default namepsace on parent & prefixed in nested => no prefixes at all
- prefixed namespace on parent & default namespace in nested => prefixes only when default one is not present
to be sure those keep working as expected.

As soon as I have executed the tests against 0.6.0 and confirmed that it was working this way I will add the `bug` label.
Update: it's confirmed: the provided test works under 0.6.0 but fails under 0.7.0
The fix was released as 0.7.5, thx for the collaboration

referenced_prs.title: Fix Refresh Token issue
referenced_prs.body:
## Description

The request is handled by the logger middleware before it reaches the auth controller's refresh function.

Since the logger middleware has direct access to the request object, any modifications made to it will also affect the refresh function in the auth controller. Therefore, the refresh token will be redacted in both the auth controller and the output that is logged.

To ensure that the refresh token is passed to the auth controller without any issues and the logged output has the refresh token redacted, a clone object can be created from the request object using the following code:
` const output = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(stdSerializers.req(request)));`

issues.body:
Running a project with Vue3 / Quasar2 / Vite in development mode fails after update.

```
// node_modules/graphql/jsutils/instanceOf.mjs

Changing

to

globalThis.process && globalThis.process.env['NODE_ENV'] === 'production'

solves the problem for me.

referenced_prs.title: fix: remove `globalThis` check and align with what bundlers can accept
referenced_prs.body:
As surfaced in [Discord](https://discord.com/channels/625400653321076807/862957336082645006/1206980831915282532) this currently is a breaking change in the 16.x.x release line which is preventing folks from upgrading towards a security fix. This PR should result in a patch release on the 16 release line.

This change was originally introduced to support CFW and browser environments which should still be supported with the `typeof` check CC @n1ru4l

This also adds a check whether `.env` is present as in the DOM using `id="process"` defines that as a global which we don't want to access on accident. as shown in https://github.com/graphql/graphql-js/pull/4017

Bundles also target `process.env.NODE_ENV` specifically which fails when it replaces `globalThis.process.env.NODE_ENV` as this becomes `globalThis."production"` which is invalid syntax.

Fixes https://github.com/graphql/graphql-js/issues/3978
Fixes https://github.com/graphql/graphql-js/issues/3918
Fixes https://github.com/graphql/graphql-js/issues/3928
Fixes https://github.com/graphql/graphql-js/issues/3758
Fixes https://github.com/graphql/graphql-js/issues/3934

This purposefully does not account for https://github.com/graphql/graphql-js/issues/3925 as we can't address this without breaking CF/plain browsers so the small byte-size increase will be expected for bundled browser environments. As a middle ground we did optimise the performance here. We can revisit this for v17.

Most bundlers will be able to tree-shake this with a little help, in https://github.com/graphql/graphql-js/issues/4075#issuecomment-2094052098 you can find a conclusion with a repo where we discuss a few.

- Next.JS by default replaces [`process.env.NODE_ENV`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/b0ab0fe85fe8c93792051b058e060724ff373cc2/packages/next/webpack.config.js#L182) you can add `typeof process` linearly
- Vite allows you to specify [`config.define`](https://vitejs.dev/config/shared-options.html#define)
- ESBuild by default will replace `process.env.NODE_ENV` but does not support replacing `typeof process`
- Rollup has a plugin for this https://www.npmjs.com/package/@rollup/plugin-replace

Supersedes https://github.com/graphql/graphql-js/pull/4021
Supersedes https://github.com/graphql/graphql-js/pull/4019
Supersedes https://github.com/graphql/graphql-js/pull/3927

> This now also adds a documentation page on how to remove all of these

issues.issue_title: Regression(?) in `sample` behavior for strings
issues.body:
Hi and thanks for the really handy library! I've had a dependency on underscore on a work project for many years now (we were using version 1.8.3) and I just merged a dependabot update which pulled in version 1.12.1 and noticed an unexpected change in the behavior of the `sample` function.

Previously, you could pass a `string` as the `list` argument, and it would be treated as an array of characters, e.g.

```es6
// with underscore 1.8.3
_.sample('abcdef', 3) // returns ["c", "f", "b"]
_.sample('abcdef', 3) // returns ["b", "e", "f"]
```

But now it just returns a substring from the beginning of the string, with no randomness

```es6
// with underscore 1.12.1+ (also tried on underscorejs.org)
_.sample('abcdef', 3) // returns "abc" every time
_.sample('abcdef', 4) // returns "abcd" every time
```

Other observations:

 - if I don't pass an `n` argument, it does return a random letter, e.g. `_.sample('abcdef')` returns `"d"` or `"a"` etc
 - it works as expected if I split the string into an array of characters e.g. `_.sample(['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e', 'f'], 3)`

issues.issue_title: Image darkening after updating to 0.32.6
issues.body: ## Question about an existing feature I'm seeing image darkening when moving from `0.31.3` to `0.32.6` or `0.33.3` for both `jpeg` and `png`. I'm using `gulp-responsive` to generate different sizes and `sharp` as the image processor. ```javascript { quality: 80, compressionLevel: 7, progressive: true, withMetadata: false, errorOnUnusedConfig: false, skipOnEnlargement: true, errorOnEnlargement: false, silent: true, } ``` ### Please provide a minimal, standalone code sample, without other dependencies, that demonstrates this question The darkening is mostly notable less on photo-like images and more for 2-3 color images.

comments.body:
The `gulp-responsive` package relies on an out-of-date version of `sharp` from 2019.

https://github.com/mahnunchik/gulp-responsive/blob/8091ebc2fd9d8fe757201600f63c3653446147bd/package.json#L49

Please can you provide the original, input images and sample code using only `sharp`, without any other dependencies, that allows someone else to reproduce.
@lovell Thanks for the response. When using only `sharp` I **do not** see the image darkening effect.

The reason it darkens is because `gulp-responsive` (and the more up-to-date version `@localnerve/gulp-responsive`) calls `image.normalize(config.normalize)` even when `config.normalize` is false.

The `normalize` (aka `normalise`) function used to accept a boolean, and now (as of v0.32.0) it doesn't. See: https://github.com/lovell/sharp/commit/d7776e3b9812d12ac158046a0b8737b50bef11f6

The change log just says "Add support to normalise for lower and upper percentiles.". It should probably mention that support for the boolean value has changed, especially since passing `false` now equals `true` (or the function should throw on invalid options, which I think is what was intended by the TSDoc comment).

issues.issue_title: directus_refresh_token missing from collection item preview
issues.body:
### Describe the Bug

When opening a collection item preview the `directus_refresh_token` cookie is not being set within the iframe. The cookie is nowhere to be found within any of the response headers. Thus, the token refresh within the preview iframe fails.

---

The following things can be assumed about the technical configuration of the setup:

- The Directus version is `10.13.2`.
- The Directus base url is `https://cms.group.test.de`.
- The Preview from the IFrame runs at `https://preview.group.test.de`.
- The environment environment variable `REFRESH_TOKEN_COOKIE_DOMAIN` is set to `.group.test.de`.
- The environment environment variable `REFRESH_TOKEN_COOKIE_SECURE` is set to `true`.
- The environment environment variable `REFRESH_TOKEN_COOKIE_SAME_SITE` is set to `None`.
- The `Directus SDK` version `17.0.2` is used to communicate with the Directus instance. The versions `^15.0.3` and `16.1.2` have also been checked against.

**Note:** The report depicts an abstract variant of the problem; However, it correctly resembles dependencies between configuration parameters at https://docs.directus.io/self-hosted/config-options.html.

---

Furthermore, the following things can be assumed:

- Setting the refresh token cookie worked fine with Directus 10.8.2 and the above parametrization when it was first implemented.
- The feature supposedly stopped working somewhere between the versions 10.8.2 and 10.13.2.
- The behaviour has been confirmed using Google Chrome 129.0.6668.103, Brave 1.70.126 and Microsoft Edge 129.0.2792.89. Brave and Microsoft Edge where checked against without any plugins being installed.

---

When searching for potential solutions the following things where checked to assure compatibility with the browsers mentioned above:

- The cookie configuration matches strict browser policies for setting cross-domain cookies (`Secure` is `true` and `SameSite` is `none`).
- The cookie domain matches the wildcard `.group.test.de` between Directus and preview domain.
- The Directus client initialization has `withCredentials` set to `true` (see client initialization within the issue reproduction description).

---

I checked the issue with three additional people before reporting it. However, it could well be the case that we've all missed something. In that case I'd be glad if you could briefly point out the issue to me so it can be fixed on my part asap. Thanks in advance!

### To Reproduce

1. Install an older version of Directus (e.g. `10.8.2`) setting the appropriate environment variable values mentioned above (please adapt to the domain of your setup).
2. Configure a preview for a collection initializing the client using the following code:
```
import { authentication, AuthenticationClient, createDirectus, rest, RestClient } from '@directus/sdk';

getClient(url: string): AuthenticationClient<any> & RestClient<any> {
  const client = createDirectus(url)
    .with(rest())
    .with(authentication('cookie', { credentials: 'include' }));

  client.refresh();

  return client;
}
```
3. Gradually update to the newest `v10` version of Directus.

**Expected (faulty) behaviour:** It should no longer be possible to read data from the Directus API.

### Directus Version

v10.13.3

### Hosting Strategy

Self-Hosted (Docker Image)

### Database

PostgreSQL 15.7

comments.body:
With Directus version 10.10 the Studio switched over to using the `session` mode by default, where both, access and refresh token have been rolled into a single session cookie, you can read about it here https://docs.directus.io/releases/breaking-changes.html#session-cookie-based-authentication.

Since it seems like you're relying on the authentication cookie to be set by the Directus Studio, I suggest switching over your configuration to the `SESSION_COOKIE_*` environment variables and using the authentication mode `'session'` instead of cookie, when setting up the `authentication` in your SDK initialization. 

Let me know if this solves the issue for you.

@hanneskuettner Thanks a lot! This is great advice. I will get to testing it straight away.

I must have not seen the change when updating instances back then since `10.10` was skipped. That one's on me. I'll quickly report back after testing to document this for future reference.
Have you verified that the user can actually access the item and fields you're trying to access in the preview code?
Yes, I have. The user in question has full administrative rights on the Directus instance so all collections should be readable. To my knowledge the administrative role cannot be restricted.

> To my knowledge the administrative role cannot be restricted.

True. If you inspect the request made within the iframe, do you see the cookies attached to the API request?

They are attached to the token refresh call (which works fine). However, when it comes to calling the items API the token is lost. It is simply not being held within the client instance for some reason. I suppose the cookie may not be able to be read because when I tried to output the `access_token` attribute of the result that the refresh promise returns then it is `null`. However, the refresh request response itself shows the `Set-Cookies` header which does also set the cookie with browser correctly.

> I suppose the cookie may not be able to be read because when I tried to output the access_token attribute of the result that the refresh promise returns then it is null.

With the session cookie that is the expected result, as the session cookie is an `HttpOnly` cookie, that the JS can't read. 

Can you give it a try without calling `refresh()`? The app/SDK should handle the cookie refresh for you automatically. The correct session cookie should be transmitted along the request to the Directus API. If you don't see that happening I strongly suspect there is some configuration problem going one, that could be related to cookie settings, CSP on your preview page, etc..

When removing the `refresh()` call the response of the items API is still the same. Sadly, I do not seem to see the expected behaviour. Not even on a local setup where Directus runs on `localhost:8055` and the preview application on `localhost:4200`. The latter being an Angular DEV server without any Content Security Policy, whatsoever. I'll go check some of these basics tomorrow again. Maybe I've missed something.

Thanks a lot for taking your time!

issues.confirmation_reasoning: A maintainer (hanneskuettner, MEMBER) explicitly explained that Directus switched to session-cookie-based auth in v10.10 and recommended switching configuration to session mode, which corroborates the reported break after upgrading. No maintainer rejected the regression and no independent community confirmations were present.

This is not a fix, but a workaroud. We should figure out what exactly goes wrong with BusyBox + ps.

Traced it — `getBorders()` in `@webpod/ingrid` hits `lines[0].spaces` without checking for empty input. BusyBox ps doesn't support `-lx` so `@webpod/ps` gets back empty/garbage output, `parseLines()` returns `[]`, and boom — TypeError on `undefined`.

Opened the upstream fixes btw:
- webpod/ingrid#11 — empty input guard in getBorders()
- webpod/ps#16 — POSIX fallback when ps -lx returns nothing

Once those land and get re-vendored, the try/catch here becomes redundant. Until then it keeps kill() from blowing up on Alpine.

issues.issue_title: Instances with type-providers are not assignable to `FastifyInstance`
issues.body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I have written a descriptive issue title
- [X] I have searched existing issues to ensure the bug has not already been reported


### Fastify version

4.7.0

### Plugin version

_No response_

### Node.js version

18.1.0

### Operating system

Linux

### Operating system version (i.e. 20.04, 11.3, 10)

Ubuntu 20.04.5 LTS

### Description

Fastify instances with an enabled type-provider are not subtypes of the base `FastifyInstance` interface.

## Example

A fastify server with type-providers enabled will not be usable as input for the `@fastify/aws-lambda` plugin, which expects a `FastifyInstance` parameter.

```ts
export default function awsLambdaFastify<TEvent, TResult = LambdaResponse>(
  app: FastifyInstance,
  options?: LambdaFastifyOptions
): PromiseHandler<TEvent, TResult>;
```

## Cause
A more detailed explanation can be found in the [reproduction repo](https://github.com/driimus/fastify-instance-assignability#cause). 

In short, the assignability issue stems from certain methods of `FastifyInstance` being contravariant on `TypeProvider`. Because of that, the compiler has to flip the assignability check's direction, which boils down to the following outcome:

```diff

### Expected Behavior

I would expect specialised versions of the `FastifyInstance` interface, such as the ones using a custom type provider, to be assignable to `FastifyInstance`.

I am aware of some available workarounds:
1. Extracting the type-provider enabled instance into a separate reference (similar to the [scoped type-provider](https://www.fastify.io/docs/latest/Reference/Type-Providers/#scoped-type-provider) docs suggestion).
1. Extending affected function signatures to include generic parameters which are propagated to their input argument of type `FastifyInstance`.

However, both of them seem inferior to ensuring that subtypes of `FastifyInstance` are assignable to the base interface. 
I haven't look at the way type providers are being used in details, but it seems possible: https://github.com/fastify/fastify/compare/77b7582...driimus:fastify:test/type-provider-contravariance

On top of that I believe there is an unwritten convention for version zero releases to use minor version changes (0.13 -> 0.14) to reflect breaking changes, and patch versions (0.13.1 -> 0.13.2) for non-breaking changes. This gives users some predictability.

issues.issue_title: Type import of non-existing path fails in Nuxt 3.16.0
issues.body:
### Environment

------------------------------
- Operating System: Linux
- Node Version:     v22.13.0
- Nuxt Version:     3.16.0
- CLI Version:      3.24.1
- Nitro Version:    2.11.8
- Package Manager:  yarn@4.8.1
- Builder:          -
- User Config:      -
- Runtime Modules:  -
- Build Modules:    -
------------------------------

### Reproduction

https://github.com/oskarols/nuxt-reproduction/tree/main

The above is a tiny monorepo with an example package and a nuxt application. Start the nuxt application in `apps/nuxt-app` to see the immediate error.

Downgrading nuxt (`yarn workspace nuxt-app add nuxt@3.15.4`) fixes the issue.

### Describe the bug

Hi 👋 

Importing a type when there is no related Typescript/JS file will fail in 3.16.0 when starting the dev server and when building the application. 

Here is the error shown when starting the dev server:
```
[4:58:24 PM]  ERROR  Pre-transform error: Failed to resolve import "example-package/types/Foobar" from "app.vue". Does the file exist?
  Plugin: vite:import-analysis
  File: /nuxt-monorepo/apps/nuxt-app/app.vue:9:28
  4  |  import { default as __nuxt_component_1 } from "/nuxt-monorepo/node_modules/nuxt/dist/app/components/welcome.vue";
  5  |  import { recordPosition as _tracerRecordPosition } from "./../../node_modules/vite-plugin-vue-tracer/dist/client/record.mjs"
  6  |  import {} from "example-package/types/Foobar";
     |                  ^
  7  |  const test = {};
  8  |  const _sfc_main = {};
```

I have narrowed this regression down to something that starts failing in 3.16.0. 

My guess is that we're not handling this scenario as part of the exsolve change in #31124. Seemingly there was some try/catch clauses that were removed as part of that change.

I think what's happening is that there is some code transformation that removes the type import, which turns the following:
```
import { type Foobar } from "example-package/types/Foobar";
```
Into
```
import { } from "example-package/types/Foobar";
```
And since there is no e.g. `Foobar.ts` in this directory, this import will fail.

comments.body: Stackblitz link for the reproduction: [Stackblitz](https://stackblitz.com/github/oskarols/nuxt-reproduction)

does it work if you write instead:

```ts
import type { Foobar } from "example-package/types/Foobar";
```

@danielroe That does work 👀 

Naively I just assumed that this was the exact same thing. May I ask why this has a different outcome?
the difference is that `import {} from ''` could have side effects, so it has to be resolved. but `import type {} from ''` can't have side effects - it's a pure type import.

@danielroe Is this considered a bug at all then or should the de-facto way to do type imports in a Nuxt project be by using `import type`?

Using the Vite boilerplate for Vue I also had issues with doing the same import. But there I could configure `verbatimModuleSyntax` in `tsconfig.json` which at least makes the dev server work. Doing a `build` however exhibits the same issue in the Vite boilerplate project as well:
```
error during build:
[commonjs--resolver] No known conditions for "./types/Foobar" specifier in "example-package" package
    at e (file:///nuxt-monorepo/node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/dep-Bid9ssRr.js:15559:25)
    at n (file:///nuxt-monorepo/node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/dep-Bid9ssRr.js:15559:650)
    at o (file:///nuxt-monorepo/node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/dep-Bid9ssRr.js:15559:1293)
    at resolveExportsOrImports (file:///nuxt-monorepo/node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/dep-Bid9ssRr.js:19569:18)
    at resolveDeepImport (file:///nuxt-monorepo/node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/dep-Bid9ssRr.js:19582:25)
    at tryNodeResolve (file:///nuxt-monorepo/node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/dep-Bid9ssRr.js:19412:18)
    at Object.resolveId (file:///nuxt-monorepo/node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/dep-Bid9ssRr.js:19185:19)
    at Object.handler (file:///nuxt-monorepo/node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/dep-Bid9ssRr.js:51754:15)
    at file:///nuxt-monorepo/node_modules/rollup/dist/es/shared/node-entry.js:22156:40
    at async PluginDriver.hookFirstAndGetPlugin (file:///nuxt-monorepo/node_modules/rollup/dist/es/shared/node-entry.js:22038:28)
``` 

The Vite documentations do explicitly state to use `import type`, but those docs were written 4 years ago. There is nothing explicitly recommending against the inline import type variant.

For anyone else running into this problem, we ended up using this lint rule: https://typescript-eslint.io/rules/no-import-type-side-effects

This way we could use ESLint to rewrite the code base quickly and ensure we don't have issues in the future.

I think you do need to do `import type` if you are not importing from a file that actually exists. I don't think this is a Nuxt-specific limitation.

If you are importing from a file that _does_ exist, it's up to you whether to use `import type`.

we have this rule in Nuxt config:

https://github.com/nuxt/eslint/blob/70d23716d2b7b0341e82fdd791d05189c1919a03/packages/eslint-config/src/configs/typescript.ts#L108

referenced_prs.title: fix(core): fix IE11 support by removing the isEmptyObject util
referenced_prs.body:
The utility doesn't check whether the passed object is actually an object, which causes an error in IE11. It was used inside mergeConfig to merge custom objects in a rather strange way, so mergeConfig has been reworked, and the utility has been completely removed as it is no longer needed. For compatibility reasons, the functionality has been re-implemented, but only for the headers config. This functionality is not available at all in the 1.x branch and its usefulness is questionable.

**BREAKING CHANGE:** merging custom objects is now supported only for the header config.

Fixes #7111
Ref #4871

### Describe the Bug

Our project is running on Astro 5.14.1 right now and uses the `experimental_AstroContainer` for a hand full of tests. As we also test some DOM stuff in our tests, we set `happy-dom` as test environment.
With the update to 5.16.0 all the tests using the `experimental_AstroContainer` component are failing with the following message:

> NoMatchingRenderer: Unable to render ``.
> No valid renderer was found for this file extension.


### What's the expected result?

The expected result is that it works as before, test are running successfully.

comments.body: I wonder if this could be caused by https://github.com/withastro/astro/pull/14715, introduced in 5.15.4. Can you try pinning to this version and retry?

I have also faced with similar issue after upgrade from 5.15.4 to 5.16.0.
Vitest tests fail with the following error: "Astro components cannot be used in the browser." Once I downgrade to 5.15.4 all is working fine.
I use ssr with react.

---
Checked v5.15.5 all good. Relatively to error I have it is related to https://github.com/withastro/astro/pull/14751
Just tested in which version the break happened in the stackblitz demo. It's version 5.15.6 which is the first one to show the `NoMatchingRenderer ` error for that concrete example.

This indeed seems to be a side effect from #14751. @delucis any idea? My guess is that on the client we cannot only return a function that errors, but maybe we need to assign some metadata. We may need to revert this and reconsider for v6
Ah interesting. I’ll take a look.

I guess it makes sense that it broke in this case. Setting `happy-dom` as the Vitest environment causes it to run the test in a Vite “client” environment rather than the default `ssr`:

> By default, `jsdom` and `happy-dom` use `client` environment, while `node` and `edge` environments use `ssr`

Of course this is a “fake” client still running on Node.js so previously this worked fine to render an Astro component even though in the real world, an Astro component can’t be rendered in a browser environment. But now we’re explicitly checking we’re in `ssr` to include the Astro component.

Given this is testing-specific there’s probably a fix we can do though. (I guess ideally Astro component tests should use the correct `ssr` environment, but if that’s a breaking change, it’s not one we should do in a patch 😄)

Thanks so far for taking care of that so quickly. With that input I could come up with a workaround by setting the vitest-environment for the tests actually using AstroContainer to node which works as expected then. 

`// @vitest-environment node` at the top of the test file fixed it for now. But that ofc only works if you do not need the happy-dom dependency in the same tests.

Thanks everyone for the discussion!

The breakage in Angular 18.2.14 comes from the introduction of BootstrapContext for server-side bootstrapping, which changes the behavior of getPlatform() and destroyPlatform() (they now return null).

For SSR apps:

Quick fix: downgrade to 18.2.13 to restore previous behavior:

Proper fix: migrate to the new SSR APIs:

Use bootstrapApplication() + renderApplication() with provideServerRendering()

Stop using getPlatform() / destroyPlatform()

TransferState works out of the box with this new approach

This ensures your app continues to work with SSR and avoids relying on deprecated APIs.

comments.body:
Hi @afaucogney! 

TL;dr - The spec says that, if a server advertises logging as a capability the client MAY send a `logging/setLevel` request. If the server does not accept that request, it can cause the initialization process to fail. Not just for the Inspector, but for _any client_ that is following the spec and chooses to send this message immediately after receiving the server capabilities.

## How we got here, and what's being done:

1) We previously [added a log level dropdown](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/pull/189) to the Inspector to allow the user to change the log level, but of course client and server must agree on the initial level for the value in that combobox to be correct. Therefore, it also sends the `logging/setLevel` message to any server that says it supports logging. That is perfectly [within spec](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/server/utilities/logging#setting-log-level).

2) We later realized that some servers are operating out-of-spec, advertising support for logging but not listening for this message. And yes, tragically, our examples in the Typescript SDK were all offenders. (**This is likely the case with all the other SDKs**, something I will be starting a campaign to fix after the next release of the Typescript SDK, see below). The result was that the server would not connect, and it was not clear why. The actual reason was that it was throwing a "Method not found" error since it had no listener for the RPC method `logging/setLevel`.

3) This is a tool for devs to make sure their servers are operating properly, so not sending the message and letting out-of spec behavior slide was not the right course of action. Consequently, I [added a change](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/pull/706) that detected the situation and explained the problem with a toast.

4) That left us in a position where **a)** our examples had problems and triggered this toast, and **b)** all server developers who advertised logging in their servers would have to implement the same boilerplate code we already had in our 'Everything' reference server in order to interact with any client that chooses to send the `logging/setLevel` message. 

5) I added [automatic log level handling](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/882) to the Typescript SDK and fixed all the examples. I also [updated the Everything](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/pull/2669) reference server, removing its boilerplate handling and using this functionality. In doing that, I realized there was no STDIO example in the SDK, and so it had slipped through the cracks. Because the stored level was mapped to session id, which STDIO does not have, it worked for SSE and StreamableHttp but not STDIO. The STDIO server would connect, but messages would not be filtered.

6) Finally, the upcoming release of the Typescript SDK will contain the [fix for STDIO](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/917), and will provide **a full and simple to implement example for other SDK maintainers to follow**.  The only thing server developers will have to do to avail themselves of the automatic log level handling will be to simply add logging to their capabilities response, and to call `sendLoggingMessage` with the parameters of the log message, rather than creating the full message and using `notification`.

Hello @afaucogney , faced same problem, as a workaround and just to test it, you can set logging =null into ServerCapabilities class like example below:
```kotlin
 val server = Server(
        Implementation(
            name = serverName,
            version = BuildInfo.VERSION//You need to build before to get this object into build/generated folder
        ),
        ServerOptions(
            capabilities = ServerCapabilities(logging = null, tools = ServerCapabilities.Tools(listChanged = true))
        )
    )
```

A community user (carlodek) also reported the same issue, and there is no maintainer rejection.

issues.issue_title: `export type` in "use server" file incorrectly registered as Server Action (v16.1.x regression)
issues.body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/xxarupakaxx/nextjs-export-type-use-server-repro

### To Reproduce

1. Clone the reproduction repository
2. `pnpm install && pnpm build`
3. Inspect the build output: `grep -o 'registerServerReference(Item[^)]*)'  .next/server/chunks/ssr/*.js`
4. You will see: `registerServerReference(Item,"7ff1db35e6b72c0c7105cc64b45ca67b9bc1c1bffe",null)`

The type `Item` (which is `export type { Item }` in the "use server" file) is incorrectly registered as a Server Action via `registerServerReference()`.

In larger projects (e.g. monorepo with many Server Action files), Turbopack generates an `actions.js` aggregation file that re-exports all registered Server Actions. Since the type doesn't exist at runtime, this causes:

```
Export TranscriptState doesn't exist in target module
```

or at runtime:

```
ReferenceError: EpicForFilter is not defined
```

### Current vs. Expected Behavior

**Current (v16.1.0+):** `export type { Foo }` in a `"use server"` file is passed to `registerServerReference()` and `ensureServerEntryExports()` in the compiled output. In small projects this silently registers `undefined`; in larger projects with Turbopack's action aggregation files, it causes build errors or runtime `ReferenceError`.

**Expected:** `export type` should be excluded from Server Action registration entirely, as it was in v16.0.3.

### Root Cause Analysis

PR #86296 ("Fix compilation of exported server functions", merged 2025-11-24, included in v16.1.0) refactored `server_actions.rs`. The new code collects exports into `export_name_by_local_id` and registers them as Server Actions in a post-pass. However, the collection step does not check `is_type_only` or `type_only`:

```rust
// In the ExportNamed handler — is_type_only is ignored by the wildcard pattern
ExportSpecifier::Named(ExportNamedSpecifier {
    orig: ModuleExportName::Ident(orig),
    exported: None,
    ..  // ← is_type_only silently ignored
}) => {
    self.export_name_by_local_id.insert(orig.to_id(), ...);
}
```

The **validation pass** correctly checks `!named.type_only` and `!s.is_type_only` (added in PR #85054), so no compile-time error is emitted. But the **registration post-pass** still picks up the type export and generates `registerServerReference()` for it.

**Evidence from the reproduction build output:**

```js
// .next/server/chunks/ssr/*.js
(0,a.i(981).ensureServerEntryExports)([c,d,e,f,g,h,i,j,Item])
// ...
(0,b.registerServerReference)(Item,"7ff1db35e6b72c0c7105cc64b45ca67b9bc1c1bffe",null)
```

`Item` here is `undefined` at runtime because it was a TypeScript type that was erased during compilation. In v16.0.3, the old code used `exported_local_ids` and only matched against actual function definitions, so type exports were naturally skipped.

### Verify canary release

- [x] I verified that the issue exists in the latest Next.js canary release

Verified on v16.1.5 (stable). Works correctly on v16.0.3.

### Provide environment information

```
Operating System: macOS 15.5
Node.js: v24.14.1
Next.js: 16.1.5
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

SWC transforms (next-custom-transforms), Server Actions

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

`next build` (Production)

### Additional context

- Works correctly in v16.0.3 (before PR #86296)
- Broke in v16.1.0 (which includes PR #86296)
- Related: #82029, PR #85054
- In small projects, `registerServerReference(undefined, ...)` silently succeeds but is incorrect. In larger projects with Turbopack's action module aggregation, it produces build errors like `Export X doesn't exist in target module`.
- Workaround: move `export type` out of `"use server"` files and import types directly from the source module.

comments.body:
## Additional note on reproduction

The minimal reproduction repo demonstrates the **incorrect code generation** — `registerServerReference(Item, ...)` is emitted for a type-only export. In this small project, the build succeeds because Turbopack inlines everything into a single chunk, so `Item` resolves to `undefined` and `registerServerReference(undefined, ...)` silently passes.

However, **in larger projects (monorepo with many Server Action files across multiple pages)**, Turbopack generates aggregation files like `.next-internal/server/app/<route>/page/actions.js` that re-export all Server Actions from separate modules:

```js
// Generated actions.js (aggregation file)
export {searchConferences as '402cb...'} from 'ACTIONS_MODULE11'
export {syncRecordingToS3 as '40c01...'} from 'ACTIONS_MODULE11'
export {TranscriptState as '7f747...'} from 'ACTIONS_MODULE11'  // ← type!
```

At this module boundary, Turbopack correctly detects that `TranscriptState` doesn't exist in the source module (because TypeScript erased it), producing:

```
The export TranscriptState was not found in module [project]/src/app/workshops/_actions/import-recording.ts [app-rsc] (ecmascript).
Did you mean to import syncRecordingToS3?
```

We confirmed this build error in our production monorepo by checking out the exact commit where `next` was bumped from 16.0.3 to 16.1.5, with `"use server"` files containing `export type { TranscriptState }`. The build fails consistently. Reverting to 16.0.3 resolves the issue.

**To summarize**: the repro shows the root cause (type exports being registered as Server Actions in compiled output), and the error manifests as a build failure in projects large enough for Turbopack to generate action aggregation files.

## Monorepo reproduction

I've created a more realistic monorepo reproduction:

**https://github.com/xxarupakaxx/nextjs-export-type-use-server-monorepo-repro**

### Setup

```bash
git clone https://github.com/xxarupakaxx/nextjs-export-type-use-server-monorepo-repro.git
cd nextjs-export-type-use-server-monorepo-repro
pnpm install
cd apps/web
pnpm build
```

### Verification

After a successful build, inspect the compiled output:

```bash
grep -o 'registerServerReference([A-Z][a-zA-Z]*,' .next/server/chunks/ssr/*.js
```

Output:

```
registerServerReference(TranscriptState,
registerServerReference(EpicForFilter,
```

Both `TranscriptState` and `EpicForFilter` are TypeScript types (`export type { TranscriptState }` and `export type { EpicForFilter }` in `"use server"` files), but they are incorrectly passed to `registerServerReference()` in the compiled output.

### Why this matters

In this small monorepo, Turbopack inlines everything so `registerServerReference(undefined, ...)` silently passes. However, in our production monorepo (with 50+ Server Action files across dozens of pages), Turbopack generates action aggregation files (`.next-internal/server/app/<route>/page/actions.js`) that re-export Server Actions across module boundaries. At that point, Turbopack detects that the type export doesn't exist in the source module:

```
The export TranscriptState was not found in module [project]/src/app/workshops/_actions/import-recording.ts [app-rsc] (ecmascript).
```

This causes a **build failure** in larger projects. We verified this by bumping Next.js from 16.0.3 → 16.1.5 in our monorepo — the build fails consistently. Reverting to 16.0.3 resolves the issue.

### Structure

```
├── packages/shared/         # Shared types and functions
│   └── src/index.ts         # Exports TranscriptState, EpicForFilter types
├── apps/web/                # Next.js 16.1.5 app
│   ├── app/lib/
│   │   ├── import-recording.ts   # "use server" + export type { TranscriptState }
│   │   ├── epics-actions.ts      # "use server" + export type { EpicForFilter }
│   │   ├── likes-actions.ts      # "use server" (normal)
│   │   ├── comments-actions.ts   # "use server" (normal)
│   │   ├── views-actions.ts      # "use server" (normal)
│   │   ├── tags-actions.ts       # "use server" (normal)
│   │   └── extra-actions-*.ts    # 10 additional "use server" files
│   ├── app/workshops/            # Page referencing many server actions
│   └── app/items/[id]/           # Dynamic route referencing many server actions
└── pnpm-workspace.yaml
```
This closed issue has been automatically locked because it had no new activity for 2 weeks. If you are running into a similar issue, please create a new issue with the steps to reproduce. Thank you.

referenced_prs.body:
Fix #56487 #35110

Locally, the issue I had was this:

```
 ⨯ ../../../node_modules/@babel/runtime/helpers/assertThisInitialized.js
Module parse failed: Cannot use 'import.meta' outside a module (41:16)
|                 // still a Refresh Boundary later.
|                 // @ts-ignore importMeta is replaced in the loader
>                 import.meta.webpackHot.accept();
|                 // This field is set when the previous version of this module was a
|                 // Refresh Boundary, letting us know we need to check for invalidation or

Import trace for requested module:
../../../node_modules/@babel/runtime/helpers/assertThisInitialized.js
../../../node_modules/react-relay/lib/ReactRelayFragmentContainer.js
../../../node_modules/react-relay/lib/index.js
../../../node_modules/react-relay/index.js
```

Replacing `global.importMeta.webpackHot` with `__webpack_module__.hot` fixed it for me locally, and seem to maybe make sense given that `__webpack_module__.hot` is used across the file without issues?

That said, I have no idea about the conceptual difference between `__webpack_module__.hot` and `global.importMeta.webpackHot`, maybe there is a reason someone used `global.importMeta.webpackHot` instead of  `__webpack_module__.hot`.

Issues with the `please add a complete reproduction` label that receives no meaningful activity (e.g. new comments with a reproduction link) are automatically closed and locked after 30 days.

We were running 13.4.1 on node v16.19.0 in our production environment, and discovered that after some volume of requests or perhaps even period of time (as short as a day and a half, as long as 5 days), some next.js servers were becoming slow to unresponsive.  New requests would take at least 5 seconds to process a response.  CPU usage in the pod was maxed out, divided roughly at 33% user and 66% system.  We discovered that requests are being proxied to a `processChild.js` child process, which is listening on a different port (is this the new App Router?). - there were over 3100 TCP connections established between the parent and `processChild.js` process

**kill_processChild.sh**
```bash
#!/bin/bash

# Find the process IDs of all processes containing the string "processChild.js" in the command path
pids=$(pgrep -f "processChild.js")

# Iterate over each process ID and kill the corresponding process
for pid in $pids; do
    echo "Killing process: $pid"
    kill "$pid"
done
```

 {

};

I'm seeing this behaviour running `next dev` starting on 13.3 and newer versions (13.4 included). This isn't happening on 13.2. Somehow this looks like it's happening whenever files are being added/removed from the FS (not sure due to my current use case) while the dev script is running.

Even after closing `next dev`, jest orphaned processes are leftover.

I'm amazed by how often my comments are flat out ignored the past few weeks on various issues. We won't be able to investigate/help based on comments saying the equivalent of "It's happening". Please share code, I can't do anything to help you otherwise.

I'll have to close this issue when there is one more comment without a reproduction as I've checked multiple times now and the processes are cleaned up correctly in the latest version.

By latest version you mean the latest RC @timneutkens ? Sorry can't help with steps to reproduce, this is happening inside a spawn call in a very specific use case so best I can do is confirm that it happens.

But please correct me if I am wrong and we should get rid of output: standalone
It seems that this isn't just a problem with appDir, my project uses pageDir, but it's also has this problem
Yeah, I know. Just wanted to say that we use standalone mode without any problems with appDirectory. The OOM/crashes are not related to this issue.

Sorry if this is actually no longer the case, and standalone mode should work fine with the App router. I just ran into this when trying to use standalone mode for this template https://github.com/medusajs/nextjs-starter-medusa. I also tried to install `next@canary` and build, but get the same error.

So without standalone mode it works fine, but when I turn it on, I get this build error
```
> Build error occurred
[Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, lstat '/Users/USERNAME/dev/nextjs-starter-medusa/.next/server/app'] {
  errno: -2,
  code: 'ENOENT',
  syscall: 'lstat',
  path: '/Users/USERNAME/dev/nextjs-starter-medusa/.next/server/app'
}
```
Well I am just unsure, you get some weird errors on start but seems like it works fine in prod,

@bjornarhagen if you are using the `pages/` directory only, perhaps you can try setting `experimental.appDir` to false? Or add an `app/` page if there's none? Thanks!

issues.issue_title: next/image produces invalid HTML according to W3C (again)
issues.body:
### Run `next info` (available from version 12.0.8 and up)

    Operating System:
      Platform: linux
      Arch: x64
      Version: #29-Ubuntu SMP Wed Jan 12 17:36:47 UTC 2022
    Binaries:
      Node: 16.13.2
      npm: 8.3.2
      Yarn: 1.22.15
      pnpm: 6.11.0
    Relevant packages:
      next: 12.0.9
      react: 17.0.2
      react-dom: 17.0.2

### What version of Next.js are you using?

12.0.9

### What version of Node.js are you using?

16.13.2

### What browser are you using?

N/A

### What operating system are you using?

N/A

### How are you deploying your application?

N/A

### Describe the Bug

Using `next@12.0.7` yields no invalid HTML errors on the [W3C Markup Validation Service](https://validator.w3.org/) about `next/image`.

After upgrading to `next@12.0.9`, there is now this kind of error:

```txt
Error: Bad value data:image/svg+xml,%3csvg xmlns=%27http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%27 version=%271.1%27 width=%271000%27 height=%271000%27/%3e 
for attribute src on element img: Illegal character in scheme data: space is not allowed.
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25207499/151701974-9545dfdc-b27b-47a4-91db-69cdb0849155.png)

There was already an error similar to this one before but that has been fixed: #18850
We might add a new e2e test or CI job to ensure that next produces valid HTML according to W3C, so it's not happening again as it is the case now...

### Expected Behavior

No errors. Valid HTML according to W3C.

### To Reproduce

1. `npx create-next-app --example image-component image-app`
2. `cd image-app`
3. `npm run build`
4. `npm run start`
5. Go to `localhost:3000` and copy/paste the HTML in [The W3C Markup Validation Service](https://validator.w3.org/) or use the [
html-w3c-validator CLI](https://github.com/Divlo/html-w3c-validator).

> 

Sure, I can open a PR (by first working to have a failing test)! :+1:
@sokra As far as I understood, the problematic line is this one:
https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/6b11a58b8fd648f50ee5870287261dee2d573442/packages/next/client/image.tsx#L599

Is adding `+` instead of space would resolve the issue?
So something like that: 
```js
sizerSvgUrl = `data:image/svg+xml,%3csvg+xmlns=%27http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%27+version=%271.1%27+width=%27${widthInt}%27+height=%27${heightInt}%27/%3e`
```

If it is what is wanted, yes I will open a PR. :smile:

PR is up: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/33825

Thanks for your help to resolve this issue, could you review the PR, please ? :smile: @sokra

issues.issue_title: unhandledRejection: TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]
issues.body:
### What version of Next.js are you using?

11.1.0

### What version of Node.js are you using?

14.17.5

### What browser are you using?

Chrome

### What operating system are you using?

Windows

### How are you deploying your application?

Vercel

### Describe the Bug

After upgrading to `next` 11.1.0, I started getting this error:

```js
error - unhandledRejection: TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]: The "string" argument must be of type string or an instance of Buffer or ArrayBuffer. Received undefined    at Function.byteLength (buffer.js:727:11)
    at ServerResponse.apiRes.end (C:\path-to-project\node_modules\next\dist\server\api-utils.js:73:41)
    at writeend (C:\path-to-project\node_modules\express-session\index.js:262:22)
    at ontouch (C:\path-to-project\node_modules\express-session\index.js:353:11)
    at C:\path-to-project\node_modules\connect-mongo\build\main\lib\MongoStore.js:339:24
    at runMicrotasks (<anonymous>)
    at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:95:5) {
  code: 'ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE'
```

The code below found in `server/api-utils.ts` is not accounting for the possibility of the first parameter `args[0]` being `undefined`. Since the if condition does not cover such scenario, calling `Buffer.byteLength` with `undefined` will result in an error because `args[0]` type is not a supported type ([supported types are: `String`, `Buffer`, `TypedArray`, `DataView`, `ArrayBuffer`](https://nodejs.org/dist./v6.3.0/docs/api/buffer.html#buffer_class_method_buffer_bytelength_string_encoding)).

```js
  apiRes.end = (...args: any[2]) => {
    if (args.length && typeof args[0] !== 'function') {
      contentLength += Buffer.byteLength(args[0])
    }
```

### Expected Behavior

No error should happen

### To Reproduce

I was able to reproduce this in my app in development that uses:
- `next` 11.1.0
- `express-session` 
- `connect-mongo` session store
- `passport`
- `next-connect`

After logging in and navigating around.

With `next` 11.0.1, this error does not occur.

referenced_prs.title: Fix for stepByStepReport: cheerio ESM import and missing screenshot capture
referenced_prs.body:
## Summary

Fix two bugs in `stepByStepReport` plugin that made it completely non-functional in v4.x (ESM):

- **cheerio ESM import:** `import cheerio from 'cheerio'` fails because cheerio 1.x removed the default export. Changed to `import * as cheerio from 'cheerio'`
- **Screenshots never captured:** `if (!step.test) return` in `persistStep()` always returned early because `step.test` property doesn't exist on the `Step` class. Replaced with `if (!currentTest) return` which correctly checks the plugin's existing `currentTest` variable

## How it was tested

- Enabled plugin with `{ enabled: true, deleteSuccessful: false }`
- Ran a UI test with multiple steps (clicks, navigation, form fills)
- Result: 55 PNG screenshots captured + working HTML slideshow report

Relates to #5351

comments.body:
## Evidence

### Bug 1: Plugin crashes on load (cheerio ESM import)

**Before fix** — `import cheerio from 'cheerio'` crashes immediately, tests cannot run at all:

```
Could not load plugin stepByStepReport from module './plugin/stepByStepReport.js':
Could not load plugin from './plugin/stepByStepReport.js': The requested module 'cheerio' does not provide an export named 'default'
Error: Could not load plugin from './plugin/stepByStepReport.js': The requested module 'cheerio' does not provide an export named 'default'
    at loadPluginAsync (file:///node_modules/codeceptjs/lib/container.js:638:11)
```

### Bug 2: Screenshots never captured (`step.test` is always undefined)

**Before fix** — after fixing only the cheerio import, the plugin loads but produces an empty report with **0 screenshots**:

```
$ ls output/record_*/
index.html          # only index.html, no PNG files
```

The generated `index.html` slideshow is completely empty — no slides, no screenshots:

![empty report](https://i.imgur.com/placeholder) <!-- see below -->

**Root cause:** `persistStep()` at line 201 checks `if (!step.test) return` but the `Step` class (`lib/step/base.js`) has no `test` property — it's never assigned anywhere in the codebase. So `!step.test` is always `true` and every screenshot is skipped.

### After fix (both changes applied)

```
$ ls output/record_*/
0000.png  0005.png  0010.png  0015.png  0020.png  0025.png  0030.png  0035.png  0040.png  0045.png  0050.png
0001.png  0006.png  0011.png  0016.png  0021.png  0026.png  0031.png  0036.png  0041.png  0046.png  0051.png
0002.png  0007.png  0012.png  0017.png  0022.png  0027.png  0032.png  0037.png  0042.png  0047.png  0052.png
0003.png  0008.png  0013.png  0018.png  0023.png  0028.png  0033.png  0038.png  0043.png  0048.png  0053.png
0004.png  0009.png  0014.png  0019.png  0024.png  0029.png  0034.png  0039.png  0044.png  0049.png  0054.png  0055.png
index.html

$ ls -la output/record_*/*.png | wc -l

```

**56 PNG screenshots** (~160KB each) captured across all test steps + a working HTML slideshow.

### Config used for testing

```js
stepByStepReport: {
  enabled: true,
  deleteSuccessful: false,
}
```

export const { getClient, query, PreloadQuery } = registerApolloClient(() => {

const registeredClient = registerApolloClient(() => {

Count: {count}

Works on iOS 16+, Chrome/Firefox desktop, and Safari desktop. ### Provide environment information ```bash Operating System: Platform: darwin Arch: arm64 Version: Darwin Kernel Version 25.4.0 Binaries: Node: 24.14.1 npm: 11.11.0 pnpm: 9.15.0 Relevant Packages: next: 16.2.6 react: 19.2.4 react-dom: 19.2.4 typescript: 5.9.3 Next.js Config: output: N/A ``` ### Which area(s) are affected? comments.body:
If you add a `console.log('tapped')` inside the `onClick` handler, does it show up in Safari’s console on iOS 15 when you tap the button? That would tell you whether the handler is being invoked at all.

If it never fires, a quick check is to temporarily replace `onClick` with `onTouchEnd` to see if any touch event reaches the element. That can help tell whether it’s an event-delegation problem in React 19 on that older WebKit, or if touch events themselves are being swallowed.

Note: AI-assisted.

@tuobi2 

Thanks for the suggestions. I added both onClick and onTouchEnd tests with a visible on-screen log and console.log. Neither event fires on iOS 15.

The console shows the actual root cause — a JS parse error before any handlers are registered:

Dev:
  SyntaxError: Unexpected token '{'
  AppDevOverlayErrorBoundary (next_dist_080cxwf.js:3631)
  ErrorBoundaryHandler (next_dist_client_0o8274i.js:1538)

Prod:
  SyntaxError: Unexpected token '{'  (0wx.c~5-ry5jx.js:1)

  Inspecting the source, the error points to static initialization blocks (static { ... }) inside Next.js internal classes:

  class AppDevOverlayErrorBoundary extends _react.PureComponent {
    static {  // ← SyntaxError on iOS 15
      this.contextType = _approutercontextsharedruntime.AppRouterContext;
    }

  static {} is ES2022 — not supported in iOS 15 Safari (requires Safari 16.4+). The bundle fails to parse entirely, so React never mounts and no event handlers are registered. onClick not firing is a symptom, not the cause.

This regression was introduced in 16.1.7 — reverting to 16.1.6 fixes it. Next.js 16.1.7+ appears to use static initialization blocks in its App Router internals without downcompiling them for older WebKit targets.

issues.issue_title: [Next 9.5.4] Symbol.prototype.description polyfill raises TypeError
issues.body: # Bug report ## Describe the bug The `Symbol.prototype.description` polyfill raises TypeError in Safari 11 or any other browser that does not support `Symbol.prototype.description` natively. ## To Reproduce 1. Open a web page that runs on Next.js 9.5.4 or 9.5.5 (https://nextjs.org is handy, or you can set up a starter app locally: `npx create-next-app nextjs-blog --use-npm --example "https://github.com/vercel/next-learn-starter/tree/a24ee6c823/learn-starter" && cd nextjs-blog && npm install next@9.5.4 && npm run dev`) 2. Open developer tools 3. Enter `Symbol.iterator.description` in the console 4. `TypeError: Cannot convert a symbol to a string` is raised ## Expected behavior `Symbol.iterator.description === 'Symbol.iterator'` ## Screenshots > ## System information - OS: iOS 11.4 - Browser: Mobile Safari 11 - Version of Next.js: 9.5.4-9.5.5 - Version of Node.js: 12.10.0 ## Additional context https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/1c4aecbeaf9de44cec3484f76d23ec8103f3bc50/packages/next-polyfill-module/src/index.js#L32-L38 `/\((.+)\)/.exec(this)[1]` will not work on any browser as `RegExp.prototype.exec` is spec'd to convert the argument to a string with the abstract operation `ToString` and `ToString(symbol)` throws a `TypeError` exception. See https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-regexp.prototype.exec and https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-tostring .

referenced_prs.title: Allow next/head to render react components
referenced_prs.body:
## ℹ️ There is an [easy "workaround" you can apply](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/17721#issuecomment-711082357) instead of using React components, which are NOT supported within next/head as of NextJS 10.2 Fixes: #17721 Fixes: #17842 Essentially, >=9.5.4 breaks compatibility for having react components within `Head`. While it's true that NextJS [never truly supported this](https://nextjs.org/docs/api-reference/next/head)... > title, meta or any other elements (e.g. script) need to be contained as direct children of the Head element, or wrapped into maximum one level of or arrays—otherwise the tags won't be correctly picked up on client-side navigations. ...this is a fundamental React principle and we should support the concept of component composition. For example, ``` const HomePage = () => ( <>
Homepage
) ``` I tracked the issue to https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/16758/files#diff-f0591f99e1e66f02b12d5f64977b579eR86 where apparently we serialize `head` data in the window object now: `window.__NEXT_DATA__`, which doesn't handle components. I'm not sure the best way to handle that, but I created logic in `head-manager.ts` to handle react components and their potential children. ## TODO - [x] Allow custom components in Head to not throw runtime errors (initial render/page load) - [ ] Allow custom components in Head to render on client navigation - [x] Update Tests - [x] Ensure component children aren't duplicated (only rendered once) - [ ] Ensure component children [aren't orphaned](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/17721#issuecomment-710078557) 🤔
